A-tc358743-hw.title: TC358743 hardware

claims.statement: TC358743XBG is an HDMI-RX to MIPI CSI-2-TX bridge. The current public Toshiba datasheet is the combined TC358743XBG/TC9590XBG document, Rev. 2.20 dated 2026-05-11, 20 pages.
claims.evidence: p.1: 'The HDMI-RX to MIPI CSI-2-TX is a bridge device that converts HDMI stream to MIPI CSI-2 TX.' Footer: '1 / 20 2026-05-11 Rev. 2.20'

verification.final_statement: TC358743XBG is an HDMI-RX to MIPI CSI-2-TX bridge. The current public Toshiba datasheet is the combined TC358743XBG/TC9590XBG document, Rev. 2.20 dated 2026-05-11, 20 pages.
verification.notes: Downloaded the PDF (HTTP 200, 722,743 bytes) and extracted its text. Page 1 says 'The HDMI-RX to MIPI CSI-2-TX is a bridge device that converts HDMI stream to MIPI CSI-2 TX.' The footer reads '1 / 20 ... 2026-05-11 Rev. 2.20'. The Toshiba TC358743XBG product page lists 'Data sheet/English [May 2026]' and shows the part as mass production.

claims.statement: The datasheet lists the HDMI receiver as HDMI-RX 1.4 and cites HDMI Specification Version 1.4a (March 4, 2010) as a reference. The receiver does not support Audio Return Channel or HDMI Ethernet Channel.

claims.statement: The public datasheet lists HDCP support only as 'Support HDCP (optional)'. The block diagram shows HDCP eFuse Keys, an Authentication Engine and an HDCP Decryption Engine. The public datasheet does not state the HDCP version.

A search of the full text found no HDCP version. One error in the researcher's evidence: 'Added comment to HDCP in Features' is in Rev 0.622 (2016-04-01), not Rev 1.0. claims.statement: The Linux tc358743 driver always configures HDCP as disabled on device-tree platforms. It sets pdata.enable_hdcp = false, which sets the MASK_MANUAL_AUTHENTICATION bit in HDCP_MODE, so the bridge does not do automatic HDCP authentication.
claims.evidence: tc358743.c:2057 'state->pdata.enable_hdcp = false;'; tc358743_set_hdmi_hdcp(): else branch 'i2c_wr8_and_or(sd, HDCP_MODE, ~MASK_MANUAL_AUTHENTICATION, MASK_MANUAL_AUTHENTICATION);'

verification.final_statement: The Linux tc358743 driver always configures HDCP as disabled on device-tree platforms. It sets pdata.enable_hdcp = false, which sets the MASK_MANUAL_AUTHENTICATION bit in HDCP_MODE, so the bridge does not do automatic HDCP authentication.
verification.notes: Checked branch rpi-6.18.y, which git ls-remote shows as the HEAD/default. tc358743.c:2057 is 'state->pdata.enable_hdcp = false;' inside tc358743_probe_of(). In tc358743_set_hdmi_hdcp() (lines 407-427) the else branch writes HDCP_MODE with MASK_MANUAL_AUTHENTICATION, and the enable branch clears it and turns on auto authentication. In regs.h, HDCP_MODE = 0x8560 and MASK_MANUAL_AUTHENTICATION = 0x02 (marked 'Not in REF_01'). The setting is called from tc358743_initial_setup().

claims.statement: Audio output is either I2S or TDM; the two share pins. I2S is a single stereo data lane, controller (master) clock mode only, 16/18/20/24-bit data, left- or right-justified MSB first, 32-bit time slots only, with a 256fs oversampling clock output. TDM is fixed at 8 channels with 32-bit slots, controller clock mode only.

claims.statement: The TC358743 is accessed over I2C with 16-bit register addresses sent MSB first. Register values are little-endian: 8, 16 or 32-bit accesses go through le32_to_cpu/cpu_to_le32. A single driver write is limited to 130 bytes (I2C_MAX_XFER_SIZE = EDID_BLOCK_SIZE + 2).
claims.evidence: i2c_rd(): 'u8 buf[2] = { reg >> 8, reg & 0xff };'; i2c_rdreg_err(): 'return le32_to_cpu(val);'; line 66 '#define I2C_MAX_XFER_SIZE  (EDID_BLOCK_SIZE + 2)'

verification.final_statement: The TC358743 is accessed over I2C with 16-bit register addresses sent MSB first. Register values are little-endian: 8, 16 or 32-bit accesses go through le32_to_cpu/cpu_to_le32. A single driver write is limited to 130 bytes (I2C_MAX_XFER_SIZE = EDID_BLOCK_SIZE + 2), i.e. 2 address bytes plus 128 data bytes.
verification.notes: Line 136 is 'u8 buf[2] = { reg >> 8, reg & 0xff };'. Line 224 is 'return le32_to_cpu(val);' and line 234 is 'cpu_to_le32(val)'. Line 66 defines I2C_MAX_XFER_SIZE (EDID_BLOCK_SIZE + 2). i2c_wr() truncates longer writes with a warning. Reads use a write-then-read i2c_transfer with no length cap.

claims.statement: CHIPID is the 16-bit register at address 0x0000. Bits [15:8] hold the chip ID (MASK_CHIPID = 0xff00) and bits [7:0] the revision ID (MASK_REVID = 0x00ff). tc358743_regs.h defines no named constant for an expected chip-ID value.
claims.evidence: tc358743_regs.h:19-21 '#define CHIPID 0x0000 / #define MASK_CHIPID 0xff00 / #define MASK_REVID 0x00ff'

verification.final_statement: CHIPID is the 16-bit register at address 0x0000. Bits [15:8] hold the chip ID (MASK_CHIPID = 0xff00) and bits [7:0] the revision ID (MASK_REVID = 0x00ff). tc358743_regs.h defines no named constant for an expected chip-ID value.
verification.notes: regs.h lines 19-21. A grep for chip/revid finds only these three defines. Because reads are little-endian, the chip-ID byte comes from byte address 0x0001 and the revision from 0x0000.

claims.statement: At probe the driver reads CHIPID with i2c_rd16_err() and requires (chipid & MASK_CHIPID) == 0, meaning the chip-ID byte must read 0x00. If the read fails or the byte is non-zero it logs 'not a TC358743 on address 0x%x' and returns -ENODEV. The revision byte is not checked; tc358743_log_status only prints it.
claims.evidence: tc358743.c:2210-2215 'if (i2c_rd16_err(sd, CHIPID, &chipid) || (chipid & MASK_CHIPID) != 0) { v4l2_info(sd, "not a TC358743 on address 0x%x\n", ...); return -ENODEV; }'; log_status: '(i2c_rd16(sd, CHIPID) & MASK_REVID)'

verification.final_statement: At probe the driver reads CHIPID with i2c_rd16_err() and requires (chipid & MASK_CHIPID) == 0, meaning the chip-ID byte must read 0x00. If the read fails or the byte is non-zero it logs 'not a TC358743 on address 0x%x' and returns -ENODEV. The revision byte is not checked; tc358743_log_status only prints it.
verification.notes: Lines 2210-2214 match. log_status (lines 1379-1382) prints 'Chip ID: 0x%02x' and 'Chip revision: 0x%02x'. This check runs after tc358743_probe_of(), which handles refclk, endpoint parsing and the optional reset. A chip-ID byte of 0x00 is a weak identity test, since many devices or bus faults could also return 0x00.

claims.statement: REFCLK (ball H5) is the reference clock input. The datasheet lists 27/26 MHz or 42 MHz, in the VDDIO2 domain (1.8 V or 3.3 V).
claims.source_title: Toshiba TC358743XBG/TC9590XBG Datasheet Rev. 2.20, Table 3.1 / Figure 3.1
claims.evidence: Table 3.1: 'REFCLK I - N Reference clock input (27/26 MHz or 42 MHz) VDDIO2 1.8 V or 3.3 V'; Fig 3.1: 'H5 REFCLK'

verification.final_statement: REFCLK (ball H5) is the reference clock input. The datasheet lists 27/26 MHz or 42 MHz, in the VDDIO2 domain (1.8 V or 3.3 V).
verification.notes: Table 3.1: 'REFCLK I - N Reference clock input (27/26 MHz or 42 MHz) VDDIO2 1.8 V or 3.3 V'. The Fig 3.1 text layer puts REFCLK at H5. The kernel header tc358743.h also says 'System clock connected to REFCLK (pin H5)'. The public datasheet gives no accuracy or jitter specification.

claims.statement: The driver requires a clock named 'refclk' and accepts only 26000000, 27000000 or 42000000 Hz. Any other rate fails probe with 'unsupported refclk rate'. It sets pll_prd = refclk_hz / 6000000 and notes that the PLL input (refclk/pll_prd) must be 6–40 MHz.
claims.evidence: tc358743.c:2072-2085 '* It must be between 6 MHz and 40 MHz, lower frequency is better. */ switch (state->pdata.refclk_hz) { case 26000000: case 27000000: case 42000000: state->pdata.pll_prd = state->pdata.refclk_hz / 6000000;' ; default: 'unsupported refclk rate: %u Hz'

verification.final_statement: The driver requires a clock named 'refclk' (devm_clk_get; on error it logs 'failed to get refclk'). It supports only 26000000, 27000000 or 42000000 Hz and sets pll_prd = refclk_hz / 6000000, giving 4, 4 or 7. A comment says the PLL input (refclk/pll_prd) must be 6–40 MHz. For any other rate it logs 'unsupported refclk rate: %u Hz', but the error path leaves ret at 0 (the value from clk_prepare_enable), so tc358743_probe_of() returns 0 and probe continues. If the chip answers the CHIPID read, tc358743_initial_setup() then calls tc358743_set_ref_clk(), which hits BUG_ON(refclk not 26/27/42 MHz). A wrong refclk rate therefore causes a kernel BUG rather than a clean probe failure.
verification.notes: Lines 2049-2085 show that 'ret = clk_prepare_enable(refclk)' succeeds with ret = 0, and the switch default runs 'dev_err(...); goto disable_clk;' without setting ret. disable_clk falls through to 'return ret' (0). tc358743_probe() only returns early when err != 0. Lines 717-719 contain the BUG_ON in tc358743_set_ref_clk(), which is reached from tc358743_initial_setup() at probe line 2267. The torvalds master copy has the same code. The rest of the original claim (accepted rates, pll_prd, the 6–40 MHz comment) is correct.

claims.statement: With integer arithmetic, pll_fbd = (bps_pr_lane / refclk_hz) * pll_prd, and the lane rate is refclk/pll_prd*pll_fbd. claims.statement: At 972 Mbps per lane, the driver's lane formula gives: 1080p60 RGB888 (2.986 Gbps) needs 4 lanes; 1080p60 UYVY (1.991 Gbps) needs 3; 1080p50 UYVY (1.659 Gbps) fits in 2; 720p60 RGB888 (1.327 Gbps) needs 2. On a 2-lane CSI-2 link, 1080p60 is therefore not possible in either format.

So on a 2-lane link at 972 Mbps (the RPi overlay default and the fastest rate with driver timing tables), 1080p60 needs more lanes than are available in either format. With link-frequency 500 MHz (999 Mbps actual at 27 MHz), the formula would return 2 lanes for 1080p60 UYVY, but that rate is 'untested', uses the 594 Mbps D-PHY timings and leaves almost no margin, so it is not a supported configuration.

The original 'not possible in either format' therefore needed the 972 Mbps qualifier.

open_questions: Is the TC358743XBG I2C address selectable, for example 0x0F/0x1F via an INT-pin strap during RESETN as on TC358749XBG (A-50)? The public TC358743XBG datasheet is silent; the DT binding and RPi overlay only use 0x0f. Resolve with the Toshiba Functional Specification (DATASHEET REQUIRED, NDA) or by HARDWARE TEST: strap INT high through 10 kΩ during reset and run i2cdetect.

What is the actual I2C maximum clock: the datasheet's 400 kHz Fast-mode, or the product brief's 2 MHz 'ultra fast mode' (A-14)? Until resolved, treat 400 kHz as the limit. Resolve with the Toshiba Functional Specification (DATASHEET REQUIRED) or a Toshiba FAE.

Which HDCP version does the 'HDCP (optional)' feature implement, and do standard TC358743XBG parts ship with eFuse HDCP keys? Licensing terms are also unknown. DATASHEET REQUIRED (Toshiba functional spec or sales/FAE). Also a HARDWARE TEST: connect an HDCP-requiring source and observe behaviour with the driver's manual-authentication setting (A-04).

What is the expected CHIPID revision byte (bits [7:0] of register 0x0000) for production silicon? The driver only checks that the chip-ID byte is 0x00. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED: read 0x0000 with i2ctransfer, or run v4l2-ctl --log-status on our board.

What are the true input timing limits beyond the driver's 640–1920 x 350–1200 and 13–165 MHz (the driver says the width/height limits are unknown)? For example 1920x1200@60 reduced blanking, and interlaced (1080i) input, which the driver cap excludes. DATASHEET REQUIRED (functional spec) and HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

The public datasheet gives no power-up sequencing, no minimum RESETN pulse width and no reset-to-I2C-ready time; the driver's 1–2 ms / 20 ms values are not Toshiba-verified (A-28). It also gives no REFCLK tolerance, jitter or duty-cycle spec, and no AC timing for I2C/I2S. DATASHEET REQUIRED (functional spec, NDA).

Which CSI-2 data types and features are available beyond the driver's RGB888 and UYVY8: YCbCr422 12-bit (MASK_YCBCRFMT_422_12_BIT), audio and InfoFrame packets carried over CSI-2 (MASK_AUDOUTSEL_CSI), and their CSI-2 data type and virtual channel IDs? DATASHEET REQUIRED (functional spec) plus KERNEL SOURCE INSPECTION of the Pi CSI-2 receivers for support.

Which bridge board will PACSCORDER use (e.g. Auvidea B10x, Geekworm C77x, or custom)? What REFCLK oscillator frequency does it fit (must be 26/27/42 MHz; 27 MHz is preferred per A-23)? Is INT wired to a Pi GPIO, how many CSI-2 lanes are routed, and is RESETN GPIO-controlled? BOARD SCHEMATIC / HARDWARE INSPECTION REQUIRED.

How does TC358743AXBG (a separate Toshiba datasheet exists, dated 2019-01-23) differ from TC358743XBG, and is it a drop-in alternative? The Toshiba PDF URL found returned HTTP 404. DATASHEET REQUIRED.

What is the product lifecycle and longevity status of TC358743XBG? The product page shows a current datasheet (May 2026) and MOQ 1500, but no explicit lifecycle or longevity statement was found. VENDOR CONFIRMATION REQUIRED (Toshiba sales).

Can the device sustain 972 Mbps/lane long-term across −30..70 °C ambient on the chosen board, given the driver's empirical FIFO level of 374 and 'untested' status for other rates (A-24, A-43)? HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED (soak test across modes and temperature).
gaps: Pi 5 / CM5 overlay: rpi-6.18.y has a separate 'tc358743-pi5' overlay (README lines 5618-5630). tc358743-pi5-overlay.dts just includes tc358743.dtsi with compatible brcm,bcm2712. On Pi 5, csi0/csi1 are rp1_csi0/rp1_csi1 (RP1 CFE, not Unicam), and the camera I2C buses are i2c_csi_dsi0 = i2c6 and i2c_csi_dsi1 = i2c4 at 100 kHz (bcm2712-rpi-5-b.dts:208-222). Pi 5 / CM5 documentation needs this, not the Pi 4 'tc358743' overlay.

Lane count per board connector: Pi 4 Model B (2 lanes) versus CM4 CAM1, Pi 5 and CM5 connectors (4 lanes?). This decides whether 1080p60 is possible at all, so it must be confirmed from official Raspberry Pi hardware documentation or product briefs (OFFICIAL-RPI DOCS REQUIRED). The README's '4lane only applicable to Compute Modules CAM1' text is copied unchanged into the Pi 5 entry and may be stale.

Driver bug: if refclk is not 26/27/42 MHz, tc358743_probe_of() logs 'unsupported refclk rate' but returns 0, and the probe then hits BUG_ON() in tc358743_set_ref_clk(). Board bring-up docs should warn that a wrong clock-frequency in DT causes a kernel BUG.

The driver does not clamp the computed CSI lane count to the DT data-lanes value. It reports csi_lanes_in_use through get_mbus_config, so on a 2-lane link a mode needing 3–4 lanes must be rejected by the receiver (unicam or rp1-cfe). Receiver behaviour needs KERNEL SOURCE INSPECTION of bcm2835-unicam and rp1-cfe.

get_mbus_config reports flags = 0 with the comment 'Support for non-continuous CSI-2 clock is missing in the driver', yet the RPi overlay sets clock-noncontinuous and tc358743_set_csi() uses that flag for TXOPTIONCNTRL. The effective clock mode on the wire needs a HARDWARE TEST or receiver-side source check.
Interlaced HDMI inputs (1080i) are rejected: timings_cap lacks V4L2_DV_BT_CAP_INTERLACED, so query_dv_timings returns -ERANGE. Product documentation should list supported and unsupported input modes.

At probe the driver defaults to CEA 640x480p59.94 timings and RGB888_1X24, and polls the IRQ status every 1000 ms (10 ms with CEC). Userspace must load an EDID (e.g. v4l2-ctl --set-edid) before any source will see HPD.

EDID content constraints: the TMDS maximum is 165 MHz and the chip is HDMI 1.4, so the EDID loaded by PACSCORDER must not advertise modes above 165 MHz or deep colour. The driver accepts up to 8 blocks (1024 B), but the datasheet describes base plus one CEA extension. A project EDID needs to be defined and tested (HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED).

TC358743 power-up sequencing between rails (VDDC/VDD_MIPI/AVDD12/AVDD33/AVDD25/VDDIO1/VDDIO2), minimum RESETN pulse width and REFCLK accuracy/jitter are not in the public datasheet (DATASHEET REQUIRED, NDA). The driver's 1–2 ms reset and 20 ms settle times are empirical.

It is unknown whether the TC358743's INT pin is also an I2C-address boot strap (0x0F/0x1F), as on the TC358749XBG. Some third-party boards may sit at 0x1F. Needs the NDA functional spec or a HARDWARE TEST (i2cdetect on the actual board). Until then, avoid strongly driving or pulling INT during reset.

HPD/+5V interface: HPDO is a 3.3 V VDDIO1 output and is not marked 5 V tolerant; HPDI is 5 V tolerant. The pin that senses source +5V (the driver reads S_DDC5V via DDC_CTL/SYS_STATUS), and whether external level shifting or a 5V divider is needed on the bridge board, cannot be established from the public datasheet (DATASHEET or board SCHEMATIC REQUIRED).

HDCP: the datasheet says 'HDCP (optional)' with eFuse keys. Which orderable suffixes, e.g. TC358743XBG(EL,NOK) on Toshiba's page versus (EL,H4) on mirrors, carry HDCP keys is unknown (TOSHIBA SALES / DATASHEET REQUIRED). Linux never enables HDCP on DT platforms, so HDCP-protected sources will not produce video.

Audio: the supported HDMI audio sample rates, and whether audio over CSI-2 (AUDOUTSEL_CSI) works with the RPi receivers, are not documented. The driver only supports 2-channel I2S, exposed through V4L2 controls TC358743_CID_AUDIO_SAMPLING_RATE / _AUDIO_PRESENT. The tc358743-audio overlay uses a dummy 'linux,spdif-dir' codec with the Pi as I2S clock consumer (2 slots × 32 bit). I2S pin voltage equals VDDIO2, which must be 3.3 V to interface with Pi GPIO 18/19/20.

CSI-2 data types on the wire (RGB888 = 0x24, YUV422 8-bit = 0x1E per the MIPI CSI-2 spec) and the receiver-side pixel formats (V4L2_PIX_FMT_RGB24/BGR24, UYVY) were not verified for unicam or rp1-cfe. The colour conversion the driver applies (RGB full range, or BT.601 limited range for UYVY via VI_REP) affects encoder colourimetry tags.

Product lifecycle: Toshiba's product page showed TC358743XBG as mass production on 2026-10-06 (minimum order 1500, part example TC358743XBG(EL,NOK)), while a search result describes the TC358749XBG as discontinued. A long-term supply and EOL check is needed for a product BOM.

Module parameters and debugfs: rpi-6.18.y and mainline tc358743.c have a 'packet_type' module parameter (default 0x87, DRM InfoFrame) and debugfs InfoFrame dumps (AVI/AUDIO/SPD/HDMI/DRM). These are useful for HDR/colorimetry diagnostics and are not covered by the claims.
design_risks: 1080p60 cannot be carried on a 2-lane CSI-2 link. At the maximum tuned rate of 972 Mbps/lane, 1080p60 UYVY needs 3 lanes and RGB888 needs 4; 1080p50 UYVY is the 2-lane ceiling (A-05, A-24, A-25, A-26). The overlay README limits 4lane to the Compute Module CAM1 connector (A-46). Platform choice (Pi 4 Model B vs CM4/Pi 5/CM5) and connector lane count decide whether 1080p60 is possible.
Input is capped at a 165 MHz TMDS/pixel clock and 1920 width in the driver (A-07, A-08). 4K, 1440p and 1080p120 sources will not be captured; the EDID must advertise only modes within these limits.

No EDID means no hotplug. The driver does not assert HPD until userspace writes an EDID (A-33), so the boot sequence must load an EDID of at most 8 blocks / 1 KB (A-31, A-32) before any source will output video.

The driver forces HDCP to manual authentication / disabled (A-04), and the HDCP capability and keys are undocumented publicly (A-03). Sources that require HDCP (streaming boxes, Blu-ray, some consoles and cameras) may output nothing or a blank screen. This also has legal and compliance implications for a recorder.

REFCLK must be exactly 26, 27 or 42 MHz or probe fails (A-21, A-22). On Raspberry Pi the clock is a DT fixed-clock, so the bridge board must carry its own oscillator (A-45). Only 27 MHz produces the exact 594/972 Mbps rates the driver's timing tables were computed for (A-23, A-24).

With the RPi overlay there is no interrupt line (A-30). The driver polls every 1000 ms, so source-change and format-change detection can lag by up to ~1 s; enabling CEC raises polling to every 10 ms of I2C traffic. Wiring INT (active-high level, A-29) to a GPIO and adding an interrupts property avoids this.

Register-level documentation (Functional Specification, settings spreadsheet, FIFO formula) is not public and is reported to be under NDA (A-42, A-43). Any behaviour beyond the mainline driver, such as audio over CSI-2, 12-bit 4:2:2, CSI-2 timing tuning or HDCP, cannot be verified from public sources (Rule 22/23).

The I2C address is effectively fixed at 0x0f in all public configurations (A-15) and selectability is unverified (A-50 covers a different part). A second TC358743, or any other 0x0f device on the same bus, would collide.

Audio over I2S is controller (master) mode only, so the TC358743 drives BCLK/LRCK and the Pi must act as an I2S consumer/slave (A-11, A-12). The driver hard-codes 2-channel I2S (A-13), so multichannel HDMI audio is not exposed. Audio clocks track the HDMI source rather than the Pi clock, which affects A/V sync and resampling in encoding and streaming.

Ambient operating range is −30..+70 °C (A-41). An enclosed recorder in a hot venue or rack must keep the chip's ambient below 70 °C. The −40..+85 °C TC9590XBG uses a different package (7x7 mm, 0.8 mm pitch, A-40) and is not footprint-compatible.

A custom board needs five supply voltages across seven rails (1.2 V core/MIPI/AVDD12, 3.3 V VDDIO1/AVDD33, 1.8 or 3.3 V VDDIO2, 2.5 V AVDD25), with tight AVDD33/AVDD12 tolerance and 80/40 mV p-p noise limits (A-36, A-37), plus a REXT 2 kΩ ±1% resistor. Reset and power sequencing are not publicly specified (open question).

The driver only offers RGB888_1X24 and UYVY8_1X16 (A-09). The encoder pipeline must accept or convert UYVY (packed 4:2:2) or 24-bit RGB; RGB888 at 1080p needs 50% more CSI-2 bandwidth than UYVY (A-25, A-26).

verification.notes: Recomputed in Python from the driver formulas (L2079, L2100, L798). 26 MHz: prd 4, fbd 88/148, giving 572e6/962e6. 27 MHz: prd 4, fbd 88/144, giving 594e6/972e6. 42 MHz: prd 7, fbd 98/161, giving 588e6/966e6. This is the driver's model, where hsck = refclk/prd*fbd. Confirming the hardware PLL equation would need the datasheet.

claims.statement: Latent bug: for an unsupported refclk rate tc358743_probe_of() logs 'unsupported refclk rate' but jumps to disable_clk with ret still 0, so probe continues and tc358743_set_ref_clk() hits BUG_ON() (kernel BUG) instead of failing cleanly.
claims.evidence: L2049 ret = clk_prepare_enable(refclk) (0 on success); L2081-2084 default: dev_err(..."unsupported refclk rate"); goto disable_clk; (ret not set); L2161 return ret; L717-719 BUG_ON(!(refclk_hz == 26000000 || == 27000000 || == 42000000));

verification.final_statement: Latent bug: for an unsupported refclk rate, tc358743_probe_of() logs 'unsupported refclk rate' and jumps to disable_clk with ret still 0 (from the successful clk_prepare_enable), so probe_of returns 0. Probe then continues. If the CHIPID read still succeeds, tc358743_initial_setup() -> tc358743_set_ref_clk() hits BUG_ON() (kernel BUG) instead of failing cleanly. The CHIPID read is likely to succeed on Raspberry Pi, where refclk is a 'fixed-clock' whose disable does not stop the physical oscillator.
verification.notes: Checked L2049 (ret = clk_prepare_enable), L2081-2084 (default: dev_err; goto disable_clk; ret is never assigned), L2156 clk_disable_unprepare and L2161 return ret. In tc358743_probe, only a non-zero err aborts. CHIPID read and update_controls run next, then tc358743_initial_setup calls tc358743_set_ref_clk (BUG_ON at L717-719) before any division by pll_prd, which is 0. The original claim left out the precondition that the I2C CHIPID read succeeds after refclk is 'disabled'. Whether the TC358743 answers I2C without REFCLK needs the datasheet or a hardware test. In practice, keep the DT clock-frequency to 26/27/42 MHz.

DDC access to the EDID is gated by HPD.

DDC access to EDID is also enabled when hotplug is enabled. */ schedule_delayed_work(&state->delayed_work_enable_hotplug, HZ / 7);

verification.final_statement: The driver never raises HDMI hotplug (HPD_CTL 0x8544 bit HPD_OUT0) unless an EDID has been written. tc358743_enable_edid() returns early ('no EDID -> no hotplug') when edid_blocks_written == 0, which is the value after probe. With an EDID and +5V present, delayed work raises HPD after HZ/7 jiffies. The driver comment says 143 ms; with integer division it is 140 ms at the RPi defconfig default HZ=250 (142 ms at HZ=1000). Per the driver comment, DDC access to the EDID is gated by HPD.

The only HPD_OUT0 set is in tc358743_delayed_work_enable_hotplug (L404), which is scheduled only from enable_edid (L456). regs.h: HPD_CTL 0x8544, MASK_HPD_OUT0 0x01. RPi defconfigs set no CONFIG_HZ and kernel/Kconfig.hz defaults to HZ_250, so 250/7 = 35 jiffies = 140 ms. That is the only correction, to the '~143 ms' figure. The DDC gating comes from a driver comment ('See register DDC_CTL') and has not been checked against the datasheet.

Whether the 594/972 Mbps D-PHY timing constants and FIFO level 374 are valid for every mode PACSCORDER needs (e.g. 1080p50 UYVY on 2 lanes, 720p50/60, 1080p24-30). Driver comment says 374 works for 'most modes on 972Mbps'. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED; Toshiba REF_02 spreadsheet would allow computing them.

Exact torvalds/linux master commit hash and the release it corresponds to. Files were fetched from the master branch on 2026-10-06 without recording the SHA. KERNEL SOURCE INSPECTION REQUIRED (git ls-remote / git log for drivers/media/i2c/tc358743.c).
Whether the TC358743 can carry audio on CSI-2 (the driver sets CONFCTL ABUFEN but selects I2S output), and what audio formats beyond 2-channel LPCM it can output. DATASHEET REQUIRED.

Behaviour with HDCP-protected sources. HDCP is disabled (manual authentication) in the DT path and HDCP registers are write-protected via s_register. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED with representative sources (laptops, ATEM program out, cameras).

How the RPi CSI receivers handle the DT 'clock-noncontinuous' flag given that tc358743 always streams a continuous clock and reports flags=0. KERNEL SOURCE INSPECTION REQUIRED (unicam/CFE bus_flags use; Topic C).

Which kernel version and RPi branch the Buildroot raspberrypi defconfigs pin, and whether CONFIG_VIDEO_TC358743 / VIDEO_TC358743_CEC and the tc358743 overlays are included. BUILDROOT TREE INSPECTION REQUIRED.

Base-DT compatible of csi1 on Pi 4/CM4 in rpi-6.18.y (expected 'brcm,bcm2835-unicam', which binds the downstream driver since the in-tree upstream copy uses 'brcm,bcm2835-unicam-upstream'). KERNEL SOURCE INSPECTION REQUIRED (bcm2711.dtsi / bcm283x.dtsi).
gaps: Module parameters are missing from the claims. tc358743.ko has 'debug' (0-3) and 'packet_type' (default 0x87 = DRM InfoFrame, written to TYP_ACP_SET 0x8706). That packet is captured in the ACP slot and exposed through debugfs infoframes (AVI, AUDIO, SPD, HDMI VS, DRM) under the v4l2 debugfs root, in a directory named after the subdev (kernel-source, tc358743.c L39-55, L2311-2315).

Unicam legacy mode vs MC mode on Pi 4/CM4. In legacy mode the subdev node is registered read-only (v4l2_device_register_ro_subdev_nodes). On that node VIDIOC_SUBDEV_S_DV_TIMINGS and ACTIVE S_FMT return -EPERM (v4l2-subdev.c L800-801, L971-972), but S_EDID is not blocked. In MC mode the video node has no EDID or DV-timings ioctls. The PACSCORDER userspace sequence (set EDID -> wait SOURCE_CHANGE -> QUERY_DV_TIMINGS -> S_DV_TIMINGS -> S_FMT -> STREAMON) must be written per mode and per platform.

Pi 5 event delivery. cfe_notify() in rp1_cfe/cfe.c L1636-1650 skips nodes that have NODE_REGISTERED set, so V4L2_EVENT_SOURCE_CHANGE from tc358743 appears not to reach CFE video nodes. On Pi 5, subscribe on the tc358743 /dev/v4l-subdevN instead. Needs a hardware test.

The driver never applies newly detected timings itself, and stored timings are zeroed on +5V loss. After every hotplug or resolution change, userspace must QUERY_DV_TIMINGS then S_DV_TIMINGS and reconfigure the receiver and video node formats. Otherwise the receiver sees mismatched frame sizes.

EDID is volatile. There is no DT property and no default EDID in the driver, and HPD stays low until userspace writes one. The PACSCORDER init system must write an EDID within the 1080p60/165 MHz capability after every boot or module load. The EDID content (e.g. limited to the timings the selected lane count can carry) is a product decision that needs documenting.

Receiver lane limits are missing. The Unicam endpoint data-lanes must be 1, 2 or 4 (bcm2835-unicam.c L3203-3213), but tc358743 may request 3 active lanes (e.g. 1080p60 UYVY or 1080p50 RGB at 972 Mbps). Whether Unicam and RP1 CFE capture correctly with 3 active of 4 configured lanes needs a hardware test.

Platform lane capability needs an official source. Pi 4B has a 2-lane camera connector, so it cannot carry 1080p60 at 972 Mbps in any format (UYVY needs 3 lanes). Whether the Pi 5 MIPI connectors are 4-lane capable, and how to enable 4 lanes with tc358743-pi5 given the README says '4lane only applicable to Compute Modules CAM1', needs official RPi documentation (Pi 5 product brief/datasheet) or a hardware test.

Polling latency. The RPi overlays define no interrupts property, so the driver polls INTSTATUS over I2C every 1000 ms. Expect up to about 1 s latency for +5V, hotplug and format-change detection. If CONFIG_VIDEO_TC358743_CEC is enabled without an IRQ, I2C polling runs every 10 ms. Wiring the TC358743 INT pin to a GPIO plus an overlay interrupts property would avoid this; the board design must say whether it is wired.

The TC358743 I2C slave address (0x0f vs 0x1f strap option), the REFCLK accuracy and jitter requirements, the minimum reset pulse width, and power-up sequencing are not covered (DATASHEET REQUIRED). The driver only uses 0x0f via the overlay and 1-2 ms reset with a 20 ms wait.

The 165 MHz pixel clock and 1920x1200 maximum come from an undisclosed 'REF_01' document. The FIFO level of 374 and the D-PHY timing constants come from 'REF_02' (Toshiba register spreadsheet). The real silicon limits need the datasheet, and the FIFO and D-PHY values need validation per mode (HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED).

Colour handling for downstream encoders. UYVY output is converted with the BT.601 limited-range matrix and reported as V4L2_COLORSPACE_SMPTE170M even for 720p/1080p sources. RGB is full range. There is no RGB quantization-range or content-type control. Encoder VUI/colour metadata must be set to match.

HDCP is disabled (manual authentication), and HDCP registers are write-protected via s_register. Behaviour when a source requires HDCP (e.g. some cameras or switchers) is not documented. Needs a hardware test with the ATEM and other target sources.

Audio path details are missing. Supported HDMI audio sample rates and formats out of I2S (2 channels, 32-bit slots), how the 'Audio sampling rate' control tracks source changes for ALSA rate matching, and whether the tc358743-audio overlay works on Pi 5 (i2s_clk_consumer = rp1_i2s1, GPIO 18-21 on RP1). HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

No V4L2_CID_LINK_FREQ or V4L2_CID_PIXEL_RATE control is exposed, and the bridge is not a CAM_SENSOR entity. libcamera camera pipelines will not handle tc358743, so PACSCORDER must drive V4L2/media-ctl directly. On Pi 5 the CFE is always Media Controller, so the media-ctl link and format setup (tc358743 -> csi2 -> video node) needs documenting with exact entity names from a running system.

Buildroot integration is unconfirmed. The topic gives no Buildroot package or defconfig fragment for the RPi kernel (BR2_LINUX_KERNEL_DEFCONFIG=bcm2711/bcm2712), dtoverlay installation (rpi-firmware overlays), config.txt lines (dtoverlay=tc358743 or tc358743-pi5, optional 4lane/media-controller/link-frequency), or the v4l-utils package (BR2_PACKAGE_LIBV4L_UTILS) that provides v4l2-ctl and media-ctl.

Remove and suspend: the driver has no runtime PM, never disables refclk after probe, and does not drop HPD on module unload. A source may keep seeing hotplug asserted after rmmod. Needs a hardware test if module reload is part of recovery procedures.

The CONFIG_OF-only DT path hard-codes the hdmi_phy_auto_reset_* and hdmi_detection_delay platform-data fields to 0 (kzalloc). Their effect on lock behaviour with marginal sources is undocumented (DATASHEET REQUIRED).
design_risks: Lane budget: the default overlay is 2-lane at 972 Mbps (data-lanes <1 2>, link-frequency 486 MHz), and Pi 4 B CSI1 is 2-lane only. 1080p60 needs 3 lanes (UYVY) or 4 (RGB888), so on 2-lane hardware stream start fails with -EINVAL from unicam/CFE. 1080p50 UYVY, 1080p30 (either format) and 720p60 fit in 2 lanes. 1080p60 requires a 4-lane CAM1 on CM4 (CM5 unconfirmed). [B-31, B-32, B-33, B-41, B-48]

The driver accepts over-bandwidth timings in s_dv_timings and set_fmt (no check against DT data-lanes). The failure surfaces only at STREAMON, so the capture app must compute lanes needed, or restrict modes, before streaming. [B-30, B-31, B-32]

The EDID controls what the source sends. v4l2-ctl's built-in 'hdmi' EDID advertises up to 1080p60, which over-subscribes 2-lane setups. PACSCORDER needs a custom EDID limited to modes that fit the lane budget and exclude interlaced formats. [B-24, B-26, B-27, B-33]

Hotplug stays deasserted until userspace loads an EDID (after each boot/driver load), so sources see no sink until then. An early-boot service must run VIDIOC_SUBDEV_S_EDID (/dev/v4l-subdevN on Pi 5; /dev/videoN also works on Pi 4 legacy unicam). [B-21, B-22, B-25]
No interlaced capture (1080i/576i/480i return -ERANGE) and no input above 1920x1200 / 165 MHz pixel clock, so no 4K. This matters for broadcast/ATEM workflows that might output 1080i. [B-26, B-27]

REFCLK must be 26, 27 or 42 MHz and should be 27 MHz. Only 27 MHz gives exact 594/972 Mbps lane rates. An unsupported rate triggers a kernel BUG_ON rather than a clean probe failure. The overlay's 27 MHz must match the board oscillator. [B-07, B-10, B-11, B-47]
Without an INT line in DT (as in the RPi overlays), hotplug, +5V and format-change detection is polled every 1000 ms. Expect up to ~1 s latency to SOURCE_CHANGE events and HPD reactions. [B-19, B-41]

The capture pipeline must handle V4L2_EVENT_SOURCE_CHANGE: the driver mutes CSI output on signal loss or timing change but does not apply new timings. Userspace must stop streaming, query_dv_timings, s_dv_timings, re-set the format (lane count may change) and restart. [B-30, B-31, B-39]

Reported frame rate and pixel clock are derived from an integer-rounded fps (FV_CNT in 0.1 ms units). 59.94/29.97/23.976 sources are indistinguishable from 60/30/24 via query_dv_timings. Recording/encoder timestamps must not rely on it. [B-28]

UYVY output uses BT.601 limited-range conversion (colorspace SMPTE170M) even for HD sources. Downstream encoders/WebRTC may need an explicit colour-matrix choice to avoid HD colour shifts. RGB888 is full range sRGB but costs 50% more bandwidth. [B-33, B-34]

Pi 5 specifics: the RP1 CFE has no EDID/DV-timings ioctls (MC/subdev-node workflow required) and falls back to a 999 Mbps D-PHY setting because tc358743 exposes no LINK_FREQ/PIXEL_RATE control. Stability at 972/594 Mbps must be validated on hardware. [B-25, B-44, B-49]

HDMI audio arrives only via I2S on GPIO18/19/20 (separate tc358743-audio overlay, 2-ch, TC358743 as clock master), not inside the CSI stream. A/V sync and I2S pin conflicts must be handled in the product design. [B-46]

Stock RPi kernels build tc358743 without CEC (CONFIG_VIDEO_TC358743_CEC unset). If CEC control (e.g. of sources/ATEM) is wanted, a custom kernel config (e.g. Buildroot) is needed, and polling then runs every 10 ms over I2C unless an IRQ is wired. [B-19, B-20]
The non-continuous clock DT flag has no effect while streaming (the driver forces a continuous clock), so receiver configuration must tolerate a continuous clock. [B-37, B-41]

Driver unload leaves HPD asserted and refclk enabled, so a source may keep sending to an unmanaged sink after rmmod. Do not rely on module reload as a reset; a reset-gpios line is the only hardware reset path. [B-13, B-40]

claims.statement: The tc358743 driver computes bps_pr_lane = 2 x link_frequencies[0]. It requires 62.5 Mbps to 1 Gbps per lane and a refclk of 26, 27 or 42 MHz, and sets pll_prd = refclk/6 MHz. It has PHY timing tables only for 594000000 and 972000000 bps; any other rate logs "untested bps per lane" and falls through to the 594 Mbps values.
claims.evidence: tc358743.c:2092-2111 "bps_pr_lane = 2 * endpoint.link_frequencies[0]; if (bps_pr_lane < 62500000U || bps_pr_lane > 1000000000U)" ... "default: dev_warn(dev, \"untested bps per lane: %u bps\\n\"...); fallthrough; case 594000000U: ... case 972000000U:"; :2075-2079 refclk 26/27/42 MHz, pll_prd = refclk_hz / 6000000

verification.final_statement: The tc358743 driver computes bps_pr_lane = 2 x link_frequencies[0]. It requires 62.5 Mbps to 1 Gbps per lane and a refclk of 26, 27 or 42 MHz, and sets pll_prd = refclk/6 MHz. It has PHY timing tables only for 594000000 and 972000000 bps; any other rate logs "untested bps per lane" and falls through to the 594 Mbps values.
verification.notes: tc358743.c:2075-2111 (rpi-6.18.y) confirms each point. pll_prd uses integer division: 27 MHz/6 MHz = 4. pll_fbd = bps/refclk*prd gives 88 at 594 Mbps and 144 at 972 Mbps, so (27M/4)*fbd reproduces exactly 594,000,000 and 972,000,000 (I recomputed this). The lane count is capped at 4 at probe ('invalid number of lanes').

claims.statement: The tc358743 driver picks its active CSI-2 lane count as DIV_ROUND_UP(width x height x fps x bpp, bps_pr_lane), with bpp=16 for MEDIA_BUS_FMT_UYVY8_1X16 and 24 otherwise. It uses active pixels only, ignoring blanking. It reports this count via get_mbus_config and never checks it against the DT data-lanes.
claims.evidence: tc358743.c:790-801 "u32 bits_pr_pixel = (state->mbus_fmt_code == MEDIA_BUS_FMT_UYVY8_1X16) ? 16 : 24; u32 bps = bt->width * bt->height * fps(bt) * bits_pr_pixel; ... return DIV_ROUND_UP(bps, bps_pr_lane);"; :1752 "cfg->bus.mipi_csi2.num_data_lanes = state->csi_lanes_in_use;"

verification.final_statement: The tc358743 driver picks its active CSI-2 lane count as DIV_ROUND_UP(width x height x fps x bpp, bps_pr_lane), with bpp=16 for MEDIA_BUS_FMT_UYVY8_1X16 and 24 otherwise. It uses active pixels only, ignoring blanking. It reports this count via get_mbus_config and never checks it against the DT data-lanes.
verification.notes: tc358743.c:790-801 and :1752 confirm. Details: bps_pr_lane inside this function is computed as (refclk_hz/pll_prd)*pll_fbd, which equals 2×link frequency for the two supported rates. fps() is DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(pixelclock/(htotal*vtotal)), so 59.94 Hz becomes 60. state->bus.num_data_lanes is used only at probe. get_mbus_config also hard-codes flags=0 ('Support for non-continuous CSI-2 clock is missing'), although TXOPTIONCNTRL follows the DT clock-noncontinuous flag.

claims.statement: The stock tc358743 overlay has no interrupts property, so the driver polls signal status with a timer instead of an IRQ. The interval is POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 1000 ms, or 10 ms when a CEC adapter exists. The RPi bcm2711_defconfig and bcm2712_defconfig set CONFIG_VIDEO_TC358743=m but do not enable CONFIG_VIDEO_TC358743_CEC.

"cma-192 CMA is 192MB (needs 1GB)"; cma-overlay.dts "size = <0x10000000>;" (256 MB); vc4-kms-v3d-pi4-overlay.dts "&frag0 { size = <((512-4)*1024*1024)>; };"; vc4-kms-v3d-pi5-overlay.dts "&frag0 { size = <(64*1024*1024)>; };"; bcm2712.dtsi:180-185 "size = <0x0 0x4000000>; /* 64MB */ ... alloc-ranges = <0x0 0x00000000 0x0 0x40000000>"

verification.final_statement: The vc4-kms-v3d overlay (and the cma overlay) take CMA size parameters cma-64, cma-96, cma-128, cma-192 ... cma-512 and cma-size (bytes, 4 MB aligned); cma-192 and above need 1 GB. Defaults: the generic cma overlay sets 256 MB, vc4-kms-v3d-pi4 sets (512-4) MB, vc4-kms-v3d-pi5 sets 64 MB, and the bcm2712 base DT CMA pool is 64 MB within the first 1 GB.
verification.notes: cma-overlay.dts has size <0x10000000> and the overrides cma-64...cma-512, cma-size and cma-default. vc4-kms-v3d-pi4-overlay.dts has &frag0 size ((512-4)*1024*1024), and vc4-kms-v3d-pi5-overlay.dts has (64*1024*1024). overlay_map.dts:542-546 maps vc4-kms-v3d to -pi4 on bcm2711 and to -pi5 on bcm2712. bcm2712.dtsi:180-186 has linux,cma 64MB with alloc-ranges 0-0x40000000. The README's 'needs 1GB' notes appear on the generic vc4-kms-v3d entry, not the -pi4 entry.

claims.statement: Open issue #6322 reports corrupted images at 1080p50 RGB24 on a 4-lane CM4, where the driver chose 3 lanes. 6by9 attributed this to the fixed FIFO trigger level (fifo_level=374), noting Toshiba's spreadsheet gives a minimum of 120, and to the lane formula using active height instead of total line time. With link-frequency=297000000, Unicam rejected the mode with "Device has requested 5 data lanes, which is >4 configured in DT".
claims.evidence: log "Lanes needed: 3 / Lanes in use: 3"; 6by9: "I suspect it's the FIFO trigger point"; "I get min 120, max 511, which implies that the driver setting of 374 isn't being set"; "it's using bt->height in the calculation, therefore the time per line ... is going to be wrong"; "unicam fe801000.csi: Device has requested 5 data lanes, which is >4 configured in DT"

verification.final_statement: Open issue #6322 reports corrupted images at 1080p50 RGB24 on a 4-lane CM4, where the driver chose 3 lanes. 6by9 attributed this to the fixed FIFO trigger level (fifo_level=374), noting Toshiba's spreadsheet gives a minimum of 120, and to the lane formula using active height instead of total line time. With link-frequency=297000000, Unicam rejected the mode with "Device has requested 5 data lanes, which is >4 configured in DT".
verification.notes: All quotes are verified in the 39 comments (still open). The reporter found that FIFO 120 (i2ctransfer to reg 0x0006) fixed 1080p50 RGB and some 720p modes, and that a full-frame formula gave 4 lanes that worked at FIFO 374. 6by9 said: 'for 1080p50 RGB, 3 lanes will work with a FIFO delay of 0, whereas 4 lanes will require a minimum of 120.' A PiKVM out-of-tree patch exists (4001-rgb24-corruption.patch), and no fix has been merged. 6by9 also states the TC358743 is EOL at Toshiba.

claims.statement: CSI-2 payload is computed with the driver's formula (active pixels only). The fps values come from pixelclock/(htotal x vtotal): 1080p60 = 148.5 MHz/(2200x1125) = 60; 1080p50 = 148.5 MHz/(2640x1125) = 50; 1080p30 = 74.25 MHz/(2200x1125) = 30. Resulting payload: UYVY 16bpp is 1.990656 Gbps (p60), 1.658880 Gbps (p50), 0.995328 Gbps (p30); RGB888 24bpp is 2.985984 Gbps (p60), 2.488320 Gbps (p50), 1.492992 Gbps (p30). Link capacity at 2 x link frequency per lane: 297 MHz (594 Mbps/lane) gives 1.188 Gbps on 2 lanes and 2.376 Gbps on 4; 486 MHz (972 Mbps/lane) gives 1.944 Gbps on 2 lanes and 3.888 Gbps on 4.
claims.source_title: Calculation; inputs: CEA timings from include/uapi/linux/v4l2-dv-timings.h, formula from tc358743.c:790-801, link freqs from tc358743.dtsi/README

The inputs are verified in v4l2-dv-timings.h: P60 148500000 88/44/148 4/5/36 (VIC 16); P50 148500000 528/44/148 4/5/36 (VIC 31); P30 74250000 88/44/148 4/5/36 (VIC 34). claims.statement: Per-line cross-check (stricter than the driver's frame-average formula) at 972 Mbps/lane. HDMI line periods: 1080p60 = 2200/148.5 MHz = 14.815 us; 1080p50 = 2640/148.5 MHz = 17.778 us; 1080p30 = 2200/74.25 MHz = 29.630 us. Transmitting one active line takes 15.80 us for UYVY and 23.70 us for RGB888 on 2 lanes, and 7.90 us and 11.85 us on 4 lanes. So 2-lane 1080p60 UYVY and 2-lane 1080p50 RGB888 cannot keep up. 2-lane 1080p50 UYVY fits with about 2.0 us of slack before LP/HS overhead (about 675 ns per 6by9's reading of Toshiba's spreadsheet). That spreadsheet's 898.12 Mbps/lane minimum for this mode leaves about 7.6% margin at 972 Mbps.

This applies on Pi 4 (expgpio 5), Pi 5 (RP1 GPIO 34/46) and CM5 (RP1 GPIO 34).

The regulator nodes (bcm2711-rpi-4-b.dts:27-32, cm4.dts:459-461, bcm2712-rpi-5-b.dts:90-102, bcm2712-rpi-cm5.dtsi:84-89) have no regulator-boot-on and no disabled status. claims.statement: On the Pi 5 downstream CFE the D-PHY is always configured for 999 Mbps when the source is TC358743 (C-31). That matches the default 972 Mbps link, but with link-frequency=297000000 (594 Mbps) the RP1 hsfreqrange setting would not match the actual lane rate.
claims.source_title: Inference from rp1_cfe/cfe.c sensor_link_rate() and dphy.c hsfreqrange table

verification.final_statement: On the Pi 5 downstream CFE the D-PHY is always configured for 999 Mbps when the source is TC358743 (C-31). That matches the default 972 Mbps link, but with link-frequency=297000000 (594 Mbps) the RP1 hsfreqrange setting would not match the actual lane rate.
verification.notes: In dphy.c the hsfreqrange table selects the first entry with mbps <= bound. 999 gives { 999, 0b011010 }; 972 falls in (949, 999] and would select the same code, so the default is effectively correct. 594 belongs in (549, 599] = 0b010111 but is programmed as 0b011010. Whether that mismatch breaks reception is HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

claims.statement: Single-frame sizes are 4,147,200 bytes for 1920x1080 UYVY and 6,220,800 bytes for RGB888/BGR3. Four capture buffers therefore take about 16.6 MB (UYVY) or 24.9 MB (RGB888). On Pi 5 that is a large share of the 64 MB vc4-kms-v3d-pi5 CMA default, which is also used by display and other DMA users.
claims.source_title: Calculation; inputs: frame geometry, bpp, CMA defaults from C-40

verification.final_statement: Single-frame sizes are 4,147,200 bytes for 1920x1080 UYVY and 6,220,800 bytes for RGB888/BGR3, so four capture buffers take about 16.6 MB (UYVY) or 24.9 MB (RGB888). On Pi 4/CM4, Unicam (videobuf2-dma-contig, no IOMMU) allocates these from CMA. On Pi 5/CM5 the DT gives the RP1 CSI nodes iommus = <&iommu5> (with CONFIG_BCM2712_IOMMU=y), and the HVS uses iommu4. So it is not established that CFE capture buffers or display buffers count against the 64 MB vc4-kms-v3d-pi5 CMA default. KERNEL SOURCE INSPECTION or a runtime measurement (/proc/meminfo CmaFree while streaming) is required.
verification.notes: I re-checked the arithmetic: 1920*1080*2 = 4,147,200; *3 = 6,220,800; ×4 = 16.59 MB and 24.88 MB (decimal). bcm2712-rpi-5-b.dts:241-249 and bcm2712-rpi-cm5.dtsi:220-226 set iommus=<&iommu5> on csi0/csi1. bcm2712.dtsi:613 sets the HVS iommus=<&iommu4>. bcm2712_defconfig:1568 has CONFIG_BCM2712_IOMMU=y. The original claim's assumption that Pi 5 capture and display both draw on the 64 MB CMA was unsupported.

open_questions: Pi 5/CM5 with dtoverlay=tc358743,link-frequency=297000000: the rp1_cfe D-PHY is set for 999 Mbps while the bridge sends 594 Mbps per lane. Is reception reliable? HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

What is the actual memory byte order for RGB888_1X24 capture on Pi 4/CM4? The downstream Unicam labels it RGB3, but #6068 reports B,G,R on current 6.18 kernels, and the downstream Unicam fix from PR #7406 is still pending. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED (capture a solid-blue HDMI frame and dump the bytes).

CM5 on CM4IO: the CM4IO CAM1 connector is wired to CM5 MIPI0 pins (rp1_csi0) with I2C on GPIO 38/39 (i2c_csi_dsi1/i2c6). The stock overlay's default pairs i2c_csi_dsi with csi1 (MIPI1), and cam0 pairs i2c_csi_dsi0 (i2c0) with csi0. Neither combination appears to match that connector. HARDWARE TEST plus a custom overlay or KERNEL SOURCE CONFIRMATION REQUIRED.

Does the chosen TC358743 board use the connector CAM_GPIO pin (power enable or reset)? With the stock overlay that pin is expected to stay low (C-51). VENDOR SCHEMATIC REQUIRED, then HARDWARE TEST (measure CAM_GPIO and the board rails).
How many CSI-2 lanes does the chosen TC358743 board route (2 on 15-pin, 4 on 22-pin), and is its refclk 27 MHz, matching the overlay's assumption? VENDOR SCHEMATIC/DATASHEET REQUIRED.

What FIFO trigger level is correct for TC358743 modes near a lane-count boundary (e.g. 1080p50 RGB888 on 3 lanes, 1280x1024@60 RGB)? Issue #6322 is still open, and the driver hard-codes fifo_level=374. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED; Toshiba's register spreadsheet (REF_02) would be needed to compute it properly.
Is the TC358743 end-of-life? 6by9 believed so (#6322), but the Toshiba product page did not show an EOL or NRND flag when fetched. VENDOR CONFIRMATION (Toshiba lifecycle notice) REQUIRED.

Is Unicam's 1 Gbps per-lane limit documented by Broadcom? Only the RPi docs give a figure for the BCM2711 Unicam; no BCM2711 Unicam datasheet was found. DATASHEET UNAVAILABLE; treat 1 Gbps/lane as the documented limit.

Do rp1-cfe capture buffers use CMA on Pi 5? The CSI nodes have iommus = <&iommu5>, so CMA sizing may matter less on Pi 5 than on Pi 4. KERNEL SOURCE INSPECTION (vb2-dma-contig with the BCM2712 IOMMU) plus a runtime /proc/meminfo CmaFree measurement REQUIRED.

On CM5IO, the official camera doc says to fit the J6 jumpers for CAM1, but the bcm2712-rpi-cm5io.dtsi comment calls i2c_csi_dsi 'The connector that needs no jumper to enable'. Which is right? HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

Does the Buildroot raspberrypi kernel package build from these rpi-6.18.y defconfigs (bcm2711_defconfig / bcm2712_defconfig), which set CONFIG_VIDEO_TC358743=m, both Unicam variants =m and both CFE variants =m? And does Buildroot install overlays/tc358743*.dtbo and overlay_map.dtb? BUILDROOT SOURCE INSPECTION REQUIRED (package/linux, board/raspberrypi*/ and configs/raspberrypi*_defconfig).
gaps: TC358743 board reference clock: the overlay hard-codes a 27 MHz refclk (cam1_clk/cam0_clk), and the driver accepts only 26, 27 or 42 MHz. Each candidate bridge board (Auvidea B101/B102, Waveshare, Geekworm C779/C790, X1301) needs its actual crystal confirmed. BOARD SCHEMATIC / DATASHEET REQUIRED.

Which candidate TC358743 boards are physically 4-lane, and with which connector and cable (15-pin same-sided FFC vs 22-pin), is not established. Per-board pinout and cable orientation are needed for the Pi 5 and CM5IO 22-pin connectors. HARDWARE/VENDOR DOC REQUIRED.

The tc358743 get_mbus_config always reports flags=0 (continuous clock, with the comment 'Support for non-continuous CSI-2 clock is missing'). The transmitter uses TXOPTIONCNTRL from the DT clock-noncontinuous flag, so the receiver may be told continuous clock while the wire is non-continuous. Impact on Unicam/CFE is unknown. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

Using dtoverlay=tc358743,4lane on a Pi 4B (only 2 lanes routed) does not fail the probe: Unicam logs 'subdevice requires 4 data lanes when 2 are supported' and adopts 4. Documentation should forbid 4lane on Pi 4B and CM4 CAM0.

Downstream Unicam in MC mode marks UYVY8_1X16 as mc_skip, so VIDIOC_ENUM_FMT filtered by mbus_code=UYVY8_1X16 returns nothing on Pi 4/CM4 even though S_FMT UYVY works. Userspace should not depend on filtered ENUM_FMT. KERNEL SOURCE INSPECTION of try_fmt/link_validate recommended.

In legacy (default) mode on Pi 4/CM4, subdev nodes are registered read-only and EDID/DV_TIMINGS go through /dev/videoN. In MC mode (media-controller param) they must go through /dev/v4l-subdevN. PACSCORDER must choose one model per platform, and Pi 5 offers MC only.

rp1_cfe accepts the legacy RGB3 + RGB888_1X24 pairing with only a dev_warn_once ('Incorrect pixel format... Fix your application'); memory order is B,G,R either way. PACSCORDER should use BGR3/BGR24 for RGB888_1X24 on Pi 5. On Pi 4/CM4, Unicam still labels it RGB24 while the bytes are B,G,R, so the encoder path needs a swap there.

rp1_cfe cfe_notify still has the inverted NODE_REGISTERED check (rpi-6.18.y cfe.c:1645), so SOURCE_CHANGE must be subscribed on the tc358743 v4l2-subdev, not /dev/video0. Without an IRQ line in the overlay, detection latency is up to the 1 s poll interval. Whether candidate boards route the TC358743 INT pin to the Pi is HARDWARE/SCHEMATIC REQUIRED.

On CM5 with CM5IO, the default (non-cam0) overlay targets CAM/DISP 1, which needs J6 jumpers. The cm5io.dtsi comment wrongly says no jumper is needed. The /dev/i2c number and subdev name (likely i2c-0 / 'tc358743 0-000f' plus an i2c-11 symlink) are unverified. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED. CM5 on CM4IO has no usable CAM0 (those pins are USB 3.0 on CM5).

The overlays README contains further stale text: the cam0 description mentions 'i2c_vc, and cam0_reg', and the tc358743-audio entry references a nonexistent 'tc358743-fast' overlay. Whether tc358743-audio (I2S on GPIO 18/19/20) works on Pi 5/CM5 (RP1 I2S) is unverified. KERNEL SOURCE INSPECTION / HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

The interlaced HDMI inputs that an ATEM or other sources might send (1080i50/59.94) are rejected: the timings cap is progressive-only. HDCP is disabled (enable_hdcp=false). The pixel clock is capped at 165 MHz. The EDID must be loaded by userspace before HPD, and PACSCORDER needs a defined EDID file listing only supported modes.

Unresolved FIFO/lane-count bugs (#6322, still open) affect RGB888 near lane-capacity limits, e.g. 1080p50 RGB on 3 of 4 lanes, 720p30 RGB and 1280x1024@60 RGB. UYVY is the safer capture format. TC358743 is reportedly EOL at Toshiba (6by9, #6322), which is a supply-chain risk.
RP1 aggregate MIPI bandwidth is 8 Gbps across both D-PHYs. The CFE's D-PHY rate for TC358743 is always the 999 Mbps fallback, which is only correct for the default 486 MHz link frequency.

Pi 5 conversion offload: pispbe/libcamera do not support the TC358743 path. The community-reported route is gstreamer1.0-pispconvert with DMABuf (DMA_DRM) caps (#7523). Pi 5 has no H.264 hardware encoder, while Pi 4/CM4 do (CM4 datasheet: H.264 1080p30 encode). Encoder capability per platform belongs in topic docs. VENDOR DOC REQUIRED.

Buildroot specifics are not covered: the kernel config symbols needed per platform (CONFIG_VIDEO_TC358743, CONFIG_VIDEO_BCM2835_UNICAM_LEGACY for Pi 4 or CONFIG_VIDEO_RP1_CFE_DOWNSTREAM for Pi 5, CONFIG_BCM2712_IOMMU), plus installing the tc358743/tc358743-pi5 dtbo files, overlay_map.dtb and config.txt through the rpi-firmware package. BUILDROOT SOURCE INSPECTION REQUIRED.

CMA sizing on Pi 4/CM4 (Unicam needs physically contiguous buffers; the vc4-kms-v3d-pi4 default is 508 MB) versus Pi 5 (CFE behind iommu5) needs a runtime measurement of CmaFree while streaming 1080p60 with 4+ buffers. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.
design_risks: Pi 4 Model B (and any 2-lane TC358743 board) cannot capture 1080p60 in either format, or 1080p50 in RGB888. The best on 2 lanes is 1080p50 UYVY or 1080p30 RGB888. A 1080p60 product requires a 4-lane path: CM4 CAM1, Pi 5, or CM5 with a 4-lane 22-pin TC358743 board (C-01, C-02, C-37, C-47, C-48, C-49).

The tc358743 driver does not reject modes that need more lanes than are wired. The failure only appears at STREAMON as -EINVAL ('Device has requested N data lanes...'). The application must check that the lanes needed for the detected DV timings and format fit the wiring before streaming (C-15, C-16, C-47).

Lowering link-frequency to 297000000 (594 Mbps) removes 1080p60/1080p50 RGB888 entirely, even on 4 lanes. On Pi 5 it also mismatches the CFE's fixed 999 Mbps D-PHY setting. Keep the default 486000000 unless hardware testing says otherwise (C-14, C-31, C-47, C-49, C-52).

Modes near a lane-count boundary are fragile. The driver ignores blanking and uses a fixed FIFO level of 374. 1080p50 RGB888 on a 4-lane CM4 has an open corruption report, and 2-lane 1080p50 UYVY has only about 7% timing margin. Prefer UYVY and validate every advertised EDID mode on real hardware (C-43, C-44, C-50).

The control model differs by platform. Pi 4/CM4 default to video-node-centric legacy Unicam, where DV timings and EDID go through /dev/videoN. Pi 5/CM5 are Media Controller only: you must enable the csi2:4 -> rp1-cfe-csi2_ch0 link and set matching pad formats with field:none, and timings and EDID go through /dev/v4l-subdevN. The capture layer needs two code paths, or Pi 4 must also run in MC mode with media-controller=1 (C-10, C-11, C-32, C-33, C-36).

The fourcc for RGB888 differs between platforms (RGB3 on downstream Unicam, BGR3 on CFE), and the real byte order is B,G,R. UYVY8_1X16 avoids both the RGB/BGR ambiguity and the CPU colour conversion, so make UYVY the default capture format (C-34, C-35, C-33).

Source-change and hotplug detection is by polling: the overlay has no IRQ and CEC is not built in the RPi defconfigs, so status is polled every 1000 ms. On Pi 5, SOURCE_CHANGE events must be subscribed on the tc358743 subdev, not the video node. Expect up to about 1 s of latency on resolution changes (C-20, C-42).

Do not hard-code device names: I2C bus numbers, /dev/mediaN, /dev/v4l-subdevN and subdev entity names (e.g. 'tc358743 10-000f' vs '11-000f' vs the older '4-000f') vary by board, connector and kernel version. Resolve them at runtime by walking the media graph (C-24, C-26, C-27, C-28).

The camera power-enable GPIO is not driven by the TC358743 overlay and is expected to stay low. A board that depends on CAM_GPIO for power or reset needs a custom overlay with a regulator or reset-gpios (C-21, C-22, C-23, C-51).

Hardware wiring hazards: the CM4IO CAM0 port and the CM5IO CAM/DISP1 port both need J6 jumpers to carry I2C. CM5 has no CM4-style CAM0, because those pins carry USB 3.0. 15-pin bridge boards on 22-pin Pi 5/CM5 connectors need correctly sided adapter cables, or power rails can short (C-03, C-05, C-06, C-45).
libcamera and rpicam-apps do not support TC358743, so the capture pipeline must use V4L2 and Media Controller directly (e.g. GStreamer v4l2src or a custom DMABUF consumer) (C-41).
CMA budget: the Pi 5 KMS default CMA is 64 MB, and 1080p RGB888 buffers are 6.2 MB each. Size CMA explicitly (e.g. vc4-kms-v3d,cma-xxx) in the product config.txt and measure it (C-40, C-53).

open_questions: HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED: can the BCM2711 encoder (/dev/video11) sustain 1080p60 (489,600 MB/s, about 2x the official 1080p30 spec) from TC358743 UYVY input at level 4.2 with stock core_freq/gpu_freq, and how much margin does gpu_freq=550 add? Measure fps, frame drops and encode latency with v4l2-ctl/GStreamer for at least 10 minutes. Officially only 1080p30 is specified (D-10, D-12, D-52), and a Raspberry Pi engineer called 1080p60 an 'edge case' (D-50).

HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED: what is the actual list from 'v4l2-ctl -d /dev/video11 --list-formats-out' on the firmware we ship? The driver takes the list from firmware at probe (D-16), and the only list found is from 2021 (D-17).

HARDWARE TEST / VENDOR CLARIFICATION REQUIRED: does UYVY input to the Pi 4 encoder cost throughput (internal firmware conversion) compared with YUV420 input, i.e. should the pipeline go capture -> video12 ISP -> encoder or capture -> encoder directly?

HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED: Pi 5/CM5 CPU load and thermals for libx264 1080p60 from TC358743 UYVY, including the UYVY->I420/NV12 conversion. Also, does the official '~30–40% CPU' for 1080p30 encode (D-30) mean the whole 4-core CPU or one core? A Raspberry Pi clarification would resolve the second part.

HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED: on Pi 5/CM5, how much CPU headroom is left for several simultaneous encodes (recording plus RTMP plus WebRTC at different bitrates)? Each output may need its own libx264 instance.

KERNEL SOURCE INSPECTION REQUIRED (drivers/media/platform/raspberrypi/pisp_be/pisp_be.c and libpisp): can PiSP BE run standalone as a memory-to-memory UYVY->YUV420/NV12 converter on Pi 5? Its format table lists UYVY, but whether its input node accepts UYVY was not checked.

VENDOR CLARIFICATION REQUIRED: what does the bcm2712-ds.dtsi comment '(unused) H264 accelerators' (D-51) refer to? There is no H.264 driver or DT node, and Raspberry Pi engineers say BCM2712 has no H.264 HW block (D-50).

KERNEL SOURCE INSPECTION REQUIRED (bcm2835-unicam driver, tc358743 topic): does the Unicam capture buffer stride for UYVY meet the encoder's 64-byte bytesperline alignment (D-22) at every supported HDMI width, especially 720-wide SD (1440 bytes is not a multiple of 64)?
SOURCE INSPECTION REQUIRED: does FFmpeg 6.1.5 (the Buildroot version) also have an MMAP-only V4L2 M2M implementation like master (D-44)? Check the 6.1.5 tarball's libavcodec/v4l2_*.c.

HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED: on a Pi 4 Buildroot image with v4l2-probe enabled, which device does GStreamer register as 'v4l2convert': /dev/video12 (ISP) or /dev/video18 (deinterlace)? Check with gst-inspect-1.0.

LEGAL/VENDOR CLARIFICATION REQUIRED: H.264 patent licensing for software encoding (libx264/openh264) on Pi 5/CM5 compared with the Pi 4 hardware encoder, and the commercial implications of GPL x264 in a shipped product.
HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED: worst-case encoded frame size (IDR) at 1080p60 and 25 Mbps on the Pi 4 encoder. Does it exceed the 768 KiB default CAPTURE sizeimage (D-23)?
gaps: HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED: whether the Pi 4/CM4 bcm2835-codec encoder sustains 1920x1080 at 60 fps (UYVY or YUV420 input, level 4.2, with and without gpu_freq overclock). Official spec is 1080p30, the driver calls levels above 4.0 possibly not real-time, and 6by9 called 1080p60 an 'edge case' on hardware encode.

HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED: Pi 5/CM5 CPU load, thermals and latency of libx264 1080p60 (ultrafast/superfast, zerolatency) including UYVY to I420/NV12 conversion. Official figures cover only 1080p30 encode from ISP (~30-40% CPU), and x264enc/libx264 do not accept UYVY.

On Pi 5/CM5 there is no bcm2835-codec ISP (video12) or v4l2convert M2M device. It is unverified whether any Pi 5 hardware block (PiSP BE via the pispbe driver, or V3D/GL) can convert TC358743 UYVY to I420/NV12 outside libcamera; otherwise conversion is CPU (videoconvert/swscale). KERNEL SOURCE INSPECTION REQUIRED for drivers/media/platform/raspberrypi/pisp_be input formats.

Capture-side constraint that sets the encode ceiling: 1080p60 UYVY from TC358743 needs 4 CSI-2 lanes. The Pi 4B camera connector exposes 2 lanes (CM4 CAM1 and Pi 5/CM5 connectors expose 4). Belongs in the capture topic but drives the encode plan; DATASHEET/official doc citation required.

CMA/memory sizing: how much CMA the codec + vc-sm-cma + capture buffers need at 1080p60 (dtoverlay=vc4-kms-v3d,cma-*), and the gpu_mem interaction on Pi 4 firmware. Not covered; official config.txt doc and testing required.

Whether Unicam (Pi 4) capture buffers exported as DMABUF meet the codec's dma-contig requirement (single contiguous chunk, 64-byte stride for UYVY/YUV420, single-plane layout) so they can be imported zero-copy into /dev/video11. Driver source suggests yes, but it needs a HARDWARE TEST with the actual TC358743 format and stride.

Licensing implications for a commercial product: x264 is GPL-2.0+ (Buildroot X264_LICENSE), and FFmpeg with --enable-gpl becomes GPL. Enabling gst-plugins-ugly x264 sets -Dgpl=enabled. openh264 needs a separate check (Buildroot has no package/openh264, HTTP 404 at master). H.264 patent licensing applies to both hardware and software encode. Legal review required.

WebRTC/RTMP stream parameters per platform. Pi 4 hardware encoder: no B-frames, all I-frames are IDR, REPEAT_SEQ_HEADER defaults off (must be enabled for streaming), max bitrate 25 Mbps, Constrained Baseline available. Pi 5 libx264: must disable B-frames (tune zerolatency or bframes=0) for WebRTC/RTMP compatibility and needs forced keyframes for PLI. No official doc collects these.

The Buildroot master Pi defconfigs pin raspberrypi/linux 6.12.61, not rpi-6.18.y. Buildroot's upstream FFmpeg 6.1.5 lacks the RPi DRM_PRIME/DMABUF encoder patch, so h264_v4l2m2m there copies frames through MMAP buffers. A product choice is needed: GStreamer v4l2h264enc with dmabuf-import, a custom V4L2 client like rpicam-apps, or porting the RPi-Distro ffmpeg patch.

bcm2712-ds.dtsi mentions '(unused) H264 accelerators' on iommu2, while engineers say BCM2712 has no H.264 block and no driver exists. Treat Pi 5 hardware H.264 as unavailable; any clarification needs an official Raspberry Pi statement.
Audio encoding (AAC/Opus) for recording/RTMP/WebRTC and its CPU cost on each platform is not covered.

The H.264 level table limits (ITU-T H.264 Table A-1: level 4.0/4.1 MaxMBPS 245,760; level 4.2 MaxMBPS 522,240) are only reflected through rpicam-apps code. Product docs should cite the ITU-T spec directly.
Pi 4/CM4 software-encode fallback performance (x264 on Cortex-A72) has no official figures. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED if hardware encode cannot reach 1080p60.

Module autoload on a custom Buildroot image: bcm2835-codec and bcm2835-isp are VCHIQ bus children and need CONFIG_BCM2835_VCHIQ plus a non-cut-down start4.elf. Module alias and udev behaviour should be verified on target.
design_risks: Pi 4/CM4: the hardware H.264 encoder is officially specified for 1080p30, the driver calls level 4.0 the hardware spec, and 1080p60 needs twice the macroblock rate. A 1080p60 capture + hardware encode product is unproven on BCM2711. Plan fallbacks (encode 1080p30 by dropping frames, or 720p60) until a hardware test passes. (D-10, D-12, D-36, D-50, D-52)

Pi 5/CM5 has no hardware H.264 (or HEVC) encoder; the bcm2835-codec /dev/video11 path does not exist there. All H.264 encoding is CPU software (libx264/x264enc/openh264). The official CPU figure is about 30–40% for 1080p30, so 1080p60 and several simultaneous outputs (record + RTMP + WebRTC) can exhaust the CPU and the thermal budget. (D-28, D-29, D-30, D-31, D-50)
HEVC encode is unavailable on all four candidate boards; both have HEVC decode only. Any H.265 output would be pure software. (D-24, D-30, D-31)

Pixel-format mismatch on Pi 5: TC358743 UYVY is accepted by the Pi 4 hardware encoder, but libx264 (FFmpeg) and x264enc/openh264enc (GStreamer) do not accept packed UYVY. That forces a per-frame conversion (CPU swscale/videoconvert, or PiSP BE if proven), which adds more CPU load at 1080p60. (D-17, D-18, D-40, D-41, D-43)

Zero-copy on Pi 4 depends on DMABUF import into a vb2-dma-contig queue. Capture buffers must be physically contiguous, and the stride must match the encoder's bytesperline alignment (64 bytes for UYVY/YUV420); otherwise import fails or a copy is needed. (D-19, D-20, D-21, D-22)

Upstream FFmpeg (the version Buildroot ships, 6.1.5) h264_v4l2m2m uses MMAP-only buffers and so copies every frame. DMABUF/DRM_PRIME input exists only in Raspberry Pi's patched FFmpeg, so a Buildroot build needs those patches, or GStreamer/direct V4L2 for zero-copy. (D-42, D-44, D-45, D-46)

Buildroot builds gst1-plugins-good with -Dv4l2-probe=false unless BR2_PACKAGE_GST1_PLUGINS_GOOD_PLUGIN_V4L2_PROBE=y. Without it v4l2h264enc and v4l2convert silently do not exist on Pi 4 images. (D-38, D-39)

Buildroot's Pi defconfigs pin raspberrypi/linux 6.12.61, not the rpi-6.18.y default branch. The kernel version must be chosen deliberately, and bcm2835-codec is downstream-only, so a mainline kernel loses Pi 4 hardware encode entirely. (D-01, D-05, D-49)

Licensing: libx264/x264enc are GPL, and FFmpeg must be built with --enable-gpl (BR2_PACKAGE_FFMPEG_GPL), which affects product licensing, especially for Pi 5 where software encoding is mandatory. (D-42, D-46, D-47)

Pi 4 firmware: the cut-down firmware (gpu_mem=16 / Buildroot VARIANT_PI4_CD) removes codecs, so the encoder disappears. Production config.txt and the Buildroot firmware variant must keep the standard or extended firmware. (D-48)

Streaming compatibility: REPEAT_SEQ_HEADER defaults to off on the Pi 4 encoder, so it must be enabled for RTMP/WebRTC/late joiners. rpicam-apps' default libx264 settings use 1 B-frame, so WebRTC/low-latency paths must use zerolatency/no-B-frames settings. (D-14, D-15, D-32, D-35, D-37)
The Pi 4 encoder's default 768 KiB compressed buffer at >720p may be too small for high-bitrate 1080p60 IDR frames; set sizeimage explicitly. (D-13, D-23)
Interlaced HDMI sources (1080i) on Pi 4 get only the 'fast' hardware deinterlace for widths above 800 px. (D-27)
Copying the published TC358743 GStreamer example as-is signals H.264 level 3.2 (h264_level=10), which is too low for 1080p30/60 streams. Set the level control explicitly (4.0/4.2). (D-36, D-54)

claims.statement: The RPi arm64 defconfigs set CONFIG_CMA=y, CONFIG_DMA_CMA=y and CONFIG_CMA_SIZE_MBYTES=5. The CMA region in use is set in the device tree: 'cma: linux,cma' (shared-dma-pool, reusable, linux,cma-default) with size 0x4000000 (64 MB) in bcm283x.dtsi, which bcm2711.dtsi includes and restricts to below 1 GB, and in bcm2712.dtsi. The 'cma' overlay offers cma-64 through cma-512 and cma-size parameters.

verification.final_statement: The RPi arm64 defconfigs set CONFIG_CMA=y, CONFIG_DMA_CMA=y and CONFIG_CMA_SIZE_MBYTES=5. The CMA region in use comes from the device tree 'cma: linux,cma' node (shared-dma-pool, reusable, linux,cma-default, size 0x4000000 = 64 MB) in bcm283x.dtsi and bcm2712.dtsi. bcm2711.dtsi sets alloc-ranges to the lower 1 GB, but bcm2711-rpi-ds.dtsi, which bcm2711-rpi-4-b.dts and bcm2711-rpi-cm4.dts include afterwards, overrides it to <0x0 0x00000000 0x30000000>, the lower 768 MB. bcm2712.dtsi sets alloc-ranges <0x0 0x00000000 0x0 0x40000000> (lower 1 GB). The 'cma' overlay offers cma-64 through cma-512, cma-size (bytes, 4 MB aligned) and cma-default.
verification.notes: The claim implied 1 GB was the effective limit on Pi 4/CM4, but the DT includes override it to 768 MB. rpi-6.18.y bcm283x.dtsi:38-43 and bcm2711.dtsi:1118-1124 (alloc-ranges 0x40000000) are as cited. bcm2711-rpi-ds.dtsi:79-81 has '&cma { /* Limit cma to the lower 768MB to allow room for HIGHMEM on 32-bit */ alloc-ranges = <0x0 0x00000000 0x30000000>; }', and bcm2711-rpi-4-b.dts:299 and bcm2711-rpi-cm4.dts:272 include it after bcm2711.dtsi. bcm2712.dtsi:180-185 has size <0x0 0x4000000> and alloc-ranges lower 1 GB. Defconfig lines 88 (CMA=y), 1775-1776 (DMA_CMA, CMA_SIZE_MBYTES=5) and CMA_AREAS=7 confirmed. Not verified: whether the firmware or other overlays such as vc4-kms-v3d change CMA at boot.
