open_questions: Can BR2_LINUX_KERNEL_INTREE_DTSO_NAMES or BR2_LINUX_KERNEL_CUSTOM_DTS_DIR build and install Raspberry Pi downstream overlays? RPi names them <name>-overlay.dts and builds them as overlays/<name>.dtbo through its own overlays/Makefile, while Buildroot expects .dtso names. Until this works, overlays come only from the rpi-firmware tarball (E-14, E-20). BUILD TEST REQUIRED.

Why does Buildroot's raspberrypi5_defconfig explicitly disable BR2_PACKAGE_RPI_FIRMWARE_INSTALL_DTB_OVERLAYS (E-15), and does enabling it on Pi 5 cause any known boot problem? BUILDROOT GIT LOG / MAILING-LIST INSPECTION plus HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

If PACSCORDER moves the Buildroot kernel to rpi-6.18.y (current default branch, E-37), which raspberrypi/firmware commit should be paired with it? Overlays and start4.elf must match the kernel/DT ABI, and Buildroot 2026.08 pins 6.12.61-era firmware 063bcab6 (E-10). Pick the firmware commit whose extra/uname_string8 matches the chosen kernel, then run HARDWARE TEST.

On Pi 4/CM4, is the default firmware variant (BR2_PACKAGE_RPI_FIRMWARE_VARIANT_PI4, start4.elf) enough for bcm2835-codec H.264 encode and bcm2835-isp, or is start4x.elf (VARIANT_PI4_X) needed? What gpu_mem is needed on 2/4/8 GB boards, given the sample config only sets gpu_mem_256/512/1024=100? OFFICIAL RPI config.txt DOC CHECK plus HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

Does Buildroot's FFmpeg 6.1.5 build enable the h264_v4l2m2m encoder (configure autodetects it; ffmpeg.mk has no explicit v4l2_m2m switch) when BR2_PACKAGE_FFMPEG_ENCODERS=all? BUILD TEST (ffmpeg -encoders on target) REQUIRED.

Exact /dev/dma_heap/* node names on the target with Buildroot's 6.12.61 kernel compared with rpi-6.18.y (E-48). The legacy name is expected to come from the DT node 'linux,cma', but this is not confirmed. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED (ls /dev/dma_heap).
Does Buildroot's forced 4K page size on Pi 5/CM5 (E-09) change rp1-cfe, PiSP or DMABUF behaviour or performance compared with Raspberry Pi OS's 16K kernel_2712? HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

Is the 64 MB default CMA (E-47) enough for the chosen pipeline? That means TC358743 capture buffers (for example 1080p60 UYVY), encoder buffers and display (vc4-kms-v3d if used). The cma overlay or vc4-kms-v3d cma-* parameter needs sizing. CALCULATION + HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

Does the tc358743 overlay shipped in LTS-era firmware 5476720d (6.6.28) work on Pi 5? There is no tc358743-pi5.dtbo and no overlay_map entry in that kernel tree (E-53). HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED. The LTS line is probably unsuitable for Pi 5/CM5.

GStreamer stays at 1.24.13 in Buildroot 2026.08 (E-31). Do the webrtcbin and rtmp2sink features PACSCORDER needs (for example the RTMP features ATEM/servers expect, or webrtcbin renegotiation) need 1.26+? GSTREAMER RELEASE NOTES REVIEW REQUIRED.
gaps: Pi 5 cannot load the TC358743 overlay as shipped. raspberrypi5_defconfig disables BR2_PACKAGE_RPI_FIRMWARE_INSTALL_DTB_OVERLAYS, and no sample config.txt contains dtoverlay=tc358743. A PACSCORDER Pi 5 build must do two things. (a) Set INSTALL_DTB_OVERLAYS=y, or ship tc358743-pi5.dtbo plus overlay_map.dtb through BR2_PACKAGE_RPI_FIRMWARE_EXTRA_FILES (verify the overlays/ subdirectory placement). (b) Supply a project config.txt with dtoverlay=tc358743. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED to confirm the overlay remap through overlay_map.dtb on Pi 5/CM5.

Kernel modules may never load. The TC358743, Unicam (legacy and upstream), RP1 CFE (upstream and downstream), bcm2835-codec and I2C drivers are all =m in the RPi defconfigs. Buildroot's default /dev management, devtmpfs only, has no module autoloading. Choose mdev, eudev or systemd-udev, or add an explicit modprobe/modules-load step. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED to confirm the DT-modalias autoload.

Toolchain kernel headers may be too old for DMA-BUF heaps. The Bootlin 'aarch64 glibc stable 2025.08-1' toolchain declares BR2_TOOLCHAIN_HEADERS_AT_LEAST_5_4. The uapi header linux/dma-heap.h first appears in torvalds v5.6 (HTTP 404 at v5.4 and v5.5, 200 at v5.6). Userspace that uses /dev/dma_heap must therefore carry its own uapi header or use a toolchain with headers of at least 5.6. VERIFY the actual sysroot header version.

DMA-BUF heap names differ by kernel. On 6.12.61 the CMA heap name comes from cma_get_name (probably 'linux,cma'). On 6.18 there are two heaps: 'default_cma_region' and the legacy name. KERNEL SOURCE INSPECTION / HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED to fix the exact /dev/dma_heap/* names the application should open.

No CMA budget has been calculated. The DT default is 64 MB. On Pi 4/CM4 it is limited to the lower 768 MB, and on Pi 5 to the lower 1 GB. No Buildroot sample config.txt sets dtoverlay=cma or vc4-kms-v3d. Calculate the budget for HDMI capture buffers (1920x1080 UYVY = 4,147,200 bytes per frame) times the buffer count, plus encoder buffers. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

CSI-2 lane bandwidth for 1080p60 is unproven. The overlay README supports only link-frequency 297000000 or 486000000 (972 Mbit/s per lane) and 2 lanes by default, with 4lane 'only applicable to Compute Modules CAM1'. Reasoning: 1920x1080x60x16 bit = 1.99 Gbit/s of active video, which exceeds 2 x 972 = 1.944 Gbit/s. 1080p60 UYVY therefore likely needs 4 lanes (CM4/CM5 CAM1), or 1080p50/30 or a different format. DATASHEET + HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED. Also unknown: whether the 4lane parameter works on the Pi 5's MIPI connectors.

Hardware encode differs by board. Official docs say Pi 5 uses software encoders, so Pi 5/CM5 needs x264 (BR2_PACKAGE_GST1_PLUGINS_UGLY_PLUGIN_X264, or FFmpeg with BR2_PACKAGE_FFMPEG_GPL + X264). Pi 4/CM4 can use bcm2835-codec (v4l2h264enc requires BR2_PACKAGE_GST1_PLUGINS_GOOD_PLUGIN_V4L2_PROBE=y). Max resolution, level and latency of the bcm2835-codec encoder, and the CPU budget for x264 on Pi 5, are not established. DATASHEET/HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

Pi 4/CM4 firmware settings for the hardware codec are unknown. It is not established which rpi-firmware variant (start4.elf vs start4x.elf) and which gpu_mem value bcm2835-codec H.264 encode needs. The Buildroot sample uses start4.elf with gpu_mem_*=100. OFFICIAL RPI DOC or HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

Kernel and firmware pins must be managed together. Buildroot 2026.08 pins raspberrypi/linux 6.12.61 (2025-12-09), while the RPi default is rpi-6.18.y (6.18.55). Kconfig semantics changed between them (VIDEO_RP1_CFE now means the upstream driver, VIDEO_RP1_CFE_DOWNSTREAM was added), and so did DMA heap naming. Moving the kernel needs: a new tarball hash in BR2_GLOBAL_PATCH_DIR for both linux and linux-headers, an rpi-firmware version that matches (rpi-firmware.mk says 'keep in sync'), and firmware-tarball overlays from the same release.

32-bit BCM2711 kernels are dropped from 6.18. Official RPi docs: 'From kernel version 6.18, 32-bit kernel builds are not supported on BCM2711 devices', so Buildroot's 32-bit raspberrypi4_defconfig and raspberrypicm4io_defconfig are not viable with a 6.18+ kernel. Only the 64-bit defconfigs are relevant.

Image sizes are too small for the media stack. The samples use a 32M boot vfat and a 120M ext4 rootfs, likely too small for GStreamer, FFmpeg, x264 and WebRTC (OpenSSL, libnice, libsrtp). A project genimage-<board>.cfg (post-image.sh picks it up automatically) and a larger BR2_TARGET_ROOTFS_EXT2_SIZE are needed. Also undecided: an A/B or read-only rootfs and update scheme.

Bootloader and flashing are outside Buildroot. The Pi 5/CM4/CM5 EEPROM bootloader version and settings are not managed by Buildroot (2026.08 has no rpi-eeprom package) and must be pinned and documented separately. CM4/CM5 eMMC flashing uses host raspberrypi-usbboot (BR2_PACKAGE_HOST_RASPBERRYPI_USBBOOT=y in the CM defconfigs).

The CM4IO/CM5IO samples put an RTC on the camera I2C bus. config_cm4io_64bit.txt and config_cm5io.txt enable dtparam=i2c_vc=on and dtoverlay=i2c-rtc,pcf85063a,i2c_csi_dsi, the same bus the tc358743 overlay uses (TC358743 at 0x0f). Document bus sharing and the CAM0 vs CAM1 choice (the cam0 overlay parameter). HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

CEC is not enabled. CONFIG_VIDEO_TC358743_CEC needs a kernel config fragment. The overlay defines no interrupt line, so whether the driver's CEC and hotplug work in polling mode needs KERNEL SOURCE INSPECTION of drivers/media/i2c/tc358743.c.

The capture pipeline differs by platform. The default tc358743 overlay puts Unicam in legacy video-node mode, while the media-controller parameter gives MC mode. Pi 5 RP1 CFE is MC-only and needs media-ctl link and format setup. EDID loading (v4l2-ctl --set-edid) and DV-timings handling must be documented per platform. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

Buildroot release choice is unresolved. 2026.08 reaches end of life in December 2026, and the next LTS is 2027.02. The current LTS 2025.02.x has no CM5 defconfig, a 6.6.28 kernel, and firmware without tc358743-pi5.dtbo. A project decision is needed on which release to base on and how to track it.

Some packages are missing from Buildroot 2026.08. It ships GStreamer 1.24.13 and no gst1-plugins-rs, so WebRTC must use webrtcbin plus application signalling code. libcamera v0.7.1 offers only the rpi/vc4 pipeline (no rpi/pisp for Pi 5), which matters only if libcamera is used. Blackmagic ATEM integration has no Buildroot package; its source and licence are unresolved.
design_risks: Pi 5 with the stock Buildroot defconfig cannot load dtoverlay=tc358743 because raspberrypi5_defconfig disables overlay installation, so the overlays/ directory and overlay_map.dtb are missing from the boot partition. The project defconfig must set BR2_PACKAGE_RPI_FIRMWARE_INSTALL_DTB_OVERLAYS=y, which also forces DTC -@ (E-15, E-14, E-43).

DT overlays (tc358743.dtbo, tc358743-pi5.dtbo, overlay_map.dtb) come from the prebuilt raspberrypi/firmware tarball, not from the kernel source Buildroot compiles. Kernel and rpi-firmware versions must be bumped together, or the overlay compatibles and labels can drift from the kernel drivers (E-14, E-20, E-10, E-53).

Buildroot LTS 2025.02.x is a poor base for PACSCORDER. It ships kernel 6.6.28 with firmware that lacks tc358743-pi5.dtbo and has no CM5 defconfig. Buildroot 2026.08 (6.12.61) is non-LTS with EOL December 2026, and the next LTS (2027.02) is months away, so a support or maintenance plan is needed (E-02, E-03, E-05, E-11, E-53, E-01).

Kconfig symbol meanings drift between RPi kernel branches. VIDEO_BCM2835_UNICAM was the downstream driver in 6.6 but is the mainline driver (binding only 'brcm,bcm2835-unicam-upstream') from 6.12, where the downstream driver became VIDEO_BCM2835_UNICAM_LEGACY. VIDEO_RP1_CFE was the downstream driver in 6.12.61 but is the mainline driver (binding only 'raspberrypi,rp1-cfe-upstream') in rpi-6.18.y, where the RP1 DT nodes are served by VIDEO_RP1_CFE_DOWNSTREAM. Any kernel config fragment or modprobe list must be rechecked on each kernel bump (E-40, E-41, E-44, E-45).

On Pi 4/CM4 the tc358743 overlay defaults to the legacy, video-node-centric Unicam mode (compatible brcm,bcm2835-unicam-legacy). The 'media-controller' parameter switches to Media Controller mode, which changes the userspace model (media-ctl pad formats compared with plain v4l2-ctl). Pi 5 RP1 CFE is Media Controller based. A single capture code path for both platforms has to account for this (E-42, E-43, E-40, E-44).

With Buildroot's default gst1-plugins-good settings (V4L2_PROBE not enabled → -Dv4l2-probe=false), GStreamer never registers v4l2h264enc or v4l2convert, so the Pi 4/CM4 hardware H.264 encoder (bcm2835-codec) is unreachable from GStreamer unless BR2_PACKAGE_GST1_PLUGINS_GOOD_PLUGIN_V4L2_PROBE=y (E-32, E-33, E-46).

Pi 5/CM5 have no hardware H.264 encoder per official docs, so recording, RTMP and WebRTC on Pi 5/CM5 need software encoding (x264 via gst1-plugins-ugly or FFmpeg). That costs CPU and latency, and x264 is GPL, which means BR2_PACKAGE_FFMPEG_GPL=y for FFmpeg and has licence implications for the product (E-52, E-36).

All media drivers, including tc358743, unicam, rp1-cfe and bcm2835-codec, are loadable modules (MEDIA_SUPPORT=m, XZ-compressed), and Buildroot's default /dev management (devtmpfs only) does not autoload modules. The image needs mdev, eudev or systemd-udev, or explicit modprobe at boot, plus kmod with XZ support (E-49, E-50, E-39).

The effective CMA pool is the 64 MB from the device tree, not CONFIG_CMA_SIZE_MBYTES=5. On BCM2711 it is also restricted to below 1 GB. HDMI capture buffers plus encoder and display buffers may exhaust it, so it will likely need the cma or vc4-kms-v3d cma-* overlay parameters in the project config.txt (E-47, E-17).

TC358743 CEC support (VIDEO_TC358743_CEC) is not enabled in the RPi defconfigs. If PACSCORDER needs HDMI CEC toward the source or ATEM, a kernel config fragment through BR2_LINUX_KERNEL_CONFIG_FRAGMENT_FILES is required (E-38, E-39, E-27).

Buildroot forces 4K pages on Pi 5/CM5 while Raspberry Pi OS ships a 16K-page kernel_2712. Behaviour and performance verified on Raspberry Pi OS may not carry over directly to the Buildroot image (E-09, E-51).

The RPi defconfigs already use BR2_GLOBAL_PATCH_DIR=board/raspberrypi/patches to hold the custom kernel tarball hash under BR2_DOWNLOAD_FORCE_CHECK_HASHES=y. A BR2_EXTERNAL project that overrides BR2_GLOBAL_PATCH_DIR must keep that directory in its space-separated list, or provide its own linux.hash, or the kernel download fails hash checking (E-21, E-25, E-22).

The /dev/dma_heap naming changes between 6.12.61 (single heap named after the CMA area) and rpi-6.18.y (default_cma_region plus an optional legacy name). Userspace that opens a heap by fixed path must handle both (E-48).

BR2_LINUX_KERNEL_CUSTOM_DTS_PATH is deprecated for 6.12+ kernels. Custom board DTS for CM4/CM5 carrier boards (for example the TC358743 wiring) should use BR2_LINUX_KERNEL_CUSTOM_DTS_DIR with a broadcom/ subdirectory (E-28).

verification.notes: udptransport.html says: 'The ATEM Software Control application communicates with the mixer over a custom UDP protocol on port 9910. Like most custom UDP protocols this is also a re-invention of TCP over UDP. It has implemented sequence numbers, retransmissions and acknowledgements and an almost perfect copy of the TCP 3-way handshake'. index.html says: 'documentation for the reverse-engineered UDP protocol of Blackmagic Design ATEM video switchers'. claims.statement: An ATEM UDP packet has a fixed 12-byte header containing flags, packet length, a 16-bit session, an acknowledgement number, a remote sequence number and a local sequence number. The flag bits are 0=Reliable, 1=SYN, 2=Retransmission, 3=Request retransmission, 4=ACK. The payload is a series of commands, each with a 16-bit length, 2 padding bytes and a 4-ASCII-character command name.
claims.source_title: OpenSwitcher docs - The low level UDP protocol
claims.evidence: "This is the header for a packet in the UDP protocol, it's always 12 bytes long." ... "sent as a 16 bit length of the field/command, 2 unknown bytes ... and 4 ASCII characters signifying the field/command type."

verification.final_statement: An ATEM UDP packet has a fixed 12-byte header. In order it holds: a 5-bit flags field, an 11-bit packet length (which includes the 12-byte header), a 16-bit session ID, a 16-bit acknowledgement number, a 16-bit field of unknown purpose, a 16-bit remote sequence number and a 16-bit local sequence number. The flag bits are 0=Reliable, 1=SYN, 2=Retransmission, 3=Request retransmission, 4=ACK. The payload is a series of commands. Each command has a 16-bit length (header included), 2 padding/unknown bytes, a 4-ASCII-character name, and then length-8 bytes of data.
verification.notes: In the OpenSwitcher header table HTML, flags has colspan=5 and packet length colspan=11 on the first row, then session (16 bits), acknowledgement number (16), 'unknown' (16), remote sequence number (16) and local sequence number (16). The original claim left out the 16-bit 'unknown' field and the bit widths. The flag bit table matches. The payload text says: '16 bit length of the field/command, 2 unknown bytes which are most likely padding and 4 ASCII characters'.

claims.statement: ATEM connection handshake: the client sends SYN with payload 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00. The switcher replies with SYN and status byte 0x02 on success, or 0x04 meaning the client must restart. After the client's ACK, the switcher sends its full state, ending with an empty packet. Reliable packets must then be ACKed.
claims.evidence: "The payload for this packet should be 0x01 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00." ... "On a successful connection this should be 0x02. If the switcher responds with 0x04 you should restart" ... "the switcher will start dumping the full state of all fields"

verification.final_statement: ATEM connection handshake: the client sends SYN with payload 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00. The switcher replies with SYN and status byte 0x02 on success, or 0x04 meaning the client must restart. After the client's ACK, the switcher sends its full state, ending with an empty packet. Reliable packets must then be ACKed.
verification.notes: The page quotes match the claim. One extra detail: the empty packet that ends the state dump must itself be answered with a specially crafted ACK, whose remote sequence number field is set to 0x61. Clients start with a random session ID and adopt the switcher-assigned ID after the handshake.

claims.statement: Per H.264 Table A-1 as encoded in FFmpeg: Level 3.1 has MaxFS 3600 MBs and MaxMBPS 108000; Level 4 has MaxFS 8192 and MaxMBPS 245760; Level 4.2 has MaxFS 8704 and MaxMBPS 522240. A 1920x1080 frame is 120x68 = 8160 MBs, which exceeds Level 3.1's MaxFS. So 1080p30 (244800 MB/s) needs at least Level 4 (level_idc 0x28), and 1080p60 (489600 MB/s) needs Level 4.2 (0x2A). A strict 42e01f negotiation does not cover 1080p.

verification.notes: h264_levels.c ('// H.264 table A-1.') rows: 3.1 = 108000/3600; 3.2 = 216000/5120; 4 = 245760/8192; 4.1 = 245760/8192; 4.2 = 522240/8704. Recomputed: ceil(1080/16) = 68, and 120 x 68 = 8160 > 3600 and > 5120, but <= 8192. 8160 x 30 = 244800 <= 245760. 8160 x 60 = 489600 > 245760 but <= 522240. 0x28 = 40 and 0x2A = 42. Corollary: the largest 16:9 mode inside Level 3.1 is 1280x720p30 (3600 MBs x 30 = 108000). Whether browsers actually reject over-level streams is a separate interop question that needs a test.

SRT is supported by the ATEM (SDK CanStreamSRT; Mini Pro spec) but is not covered by the claims. Buildroot libsrt availability (no 'srt'-named Buildroot package was searched for), GStreamer srtsrc/srtsink (gst1-plugins-bad), and the SRT caller/listener mode ATEM uses were not established.

WebRTC signalling and ingest standards (WHIP RFC 9725 / WHEP draft), and the ICE/STUN/TURN requirements for browsers reaching PACSCORDER across NAT (MediaMTX webrtcLocalUDPAddress :8189, ICE servers), were not sourced.

Network ports PACSCORDER must document: UDP 9910 outbound to the ATEM (control/tally), TCP 1935 inbound if it hosts an RTMP server, the WebRTC ports (8889/TCP HTTP, 8189/UDP ICE in MediaMTX defaults), and any conflicts if PACSCORDER both receives RTMP from the ATEM and pushes RTMP onward.
design_risks: There is no official Linux ATEM SDK: the Switcher SDK and its runtime are Windows/macOS only (F-01, F-02, F-04). PACSCORDER must use the reverse-engineered UDP 9910 protocol (F-10, F-11, F-12, F-13) through a third-party library, with no vendor support.

ATEM firmware updates can break third-party protocol libraries (F-15). atem-connection's protocol enum stops at 2.32 (V9_6) while Blackmagic ships 10.x software (F-18), and PyATEMMax has had no release since 2022 and lacks recording/streaming status decoding (F-19, F-20). Firmware must be pinned or re-tested on every update.

Licence choice for the ATEM control library: atem-connection is MIT but needs a Node.js runtime on the target (F-14). PyATEMMax is GPL-3.0 (F-19). pyatem is LGPL-3.0-only with GPL-3.0 tools (F-21). LibAtem is LGPL-3.0 and needs .NET (F-22). This affects firmware licensing and image size.

ATEM Mini Pro HDMI out defaults to MULTIVIEW, not program (F-25). An external HDMI recorder capturing it through TC358743 records the multiview unless the output is routed to Program on the front panel, in ATEM Software Control, or possibly over UDP via aux routing 'CAuS' (F-17; unverified).

ATEM HDMI output is 1080p only, 23.98 to 60 fps, 4:2:2 10-bit (F-23). The TC358743/CSI-2 capture path on the chosen Pi must handle 1080p50/59.94/60 or the ATEM video standard must be restricted. No 720p fallback exists on the ATEM output side.
ATEM Mini Pro program audio leaves only as HDMI-embedded (or USB) audio (F-24). Recording program audio therefore depends on TC358743 HDMI audio extraction (I2S) and its ALSA integration on the Pi.

RTMP in legacy FLV carries only H.264 (CodecID 7) plus AAC (SoundFormat 10) (F-31). The ATEM SDK states the switcher may stream H.265 (F-06), which needs Enhanced RTMP on the receiver (F-31, F-32, F-34). flvmux also needs AVC-format H.264 and raw AAC, so a parser is needed after V4L2 encoders (F-34, F-35).

To receive the ATEM's RTMP push, PACSCORDER must run an RTMP server (F-46). GStreamer rtmp2src cannot listen (F-33), so MediaMTX or FFmpeg -listen is needed. MediaMTX and gst-plugins-rs have no Buildroot packages (F-43, F-44) and would need external br2 packages.

WebRTC browser interop: audio must be Opus or G.711 (F-41, F-45), so AAC from the ATEM or the local encoder must be transcoded. H.264 must have no B-frames (F-45), be Constrained-Baseline-compatible (F-36, F-39), carry SPS/PPS in-band (F-36), and signal a level that covers 1080p (Level 4.0/4.2), not the common 42e01f/Level 3.1 (F-38, F-40, F-37).

The webrtcbin route in Buildroot pulls in libnice, DTLS, SCTP and SRTP and requires dynamic libraries (F-42). The application must supply its own signalling (F-42), or use webrtcsink (MPL-2.0, not packaged in Buildroot) (F-43) or MediaMTX WHEP (F-44, F-45).

ATEM Streaming Bridge officially accepts RTMP only from Blackmagic sources (Web Presenter, ATEM Mini, ATEM SDI) (F-28), and ATEM Mini Extreme ISO G2 remote sources are limited to compatible Blackmagic cameras (F-29). Sending video from PACSCORDER into the ATEM ecosystem over the network is undocumented and may not work.

claims.statement: The tc358743 device tree overlay (rpi-6.18.y) targets the Toshiba TC358743 HDMI-to-CSI-2 bridge on Unicam 1. It is loaded with 'dtoverlay=tc358743,<param>=<val>' and takes these parameters: 4lane (Compute Module CAM1 only), link-frequency (only 297000000 or 486000000; 486000000 is the default), media-controller (default off), and cam0.

Load: dtoverlay=tc358743,<param>=<val> / Params: 4lane Use 4 lanes (only applicable to Compute Modules CAM1 connector). link-frequency ... Only values of 297000000 (574Mbit/s) and 486000000 (972Mbit/s - default) are supported by the driver. media-controller Configure use of Media Controller API ... (default off) cam0 Adopt the default configuration for CAM0 on a Compute Module (CSI0, i2c_vc, and cam0_reg).'

verification.final_statement: In rpi-6.18.y, the tc358743 overlay ('Toshiba TC358743 HDMI to CSI-2 bridge chip. Uses Unicam 1') is loaded with 'dtoverlay=tc358743,<param>=<val>'. Its parameters are 4lane (Compute Module CAM1 only), link-frequency (only 297000000 or 486000000; 486000000 is the default), media-controller (default off) and cam0. By default the overlay sets the csi1 compatible to 'brcm,bcm2835-unicam-legacy', which uses the video-node (non-MC) mode. The media-controller parameter turns that fragment off.
verification.notes: README text checked verbatim. The overlay source tc358743-overlay.dts has legacy_frag fragment@100 and media-controller = <0>,"!100". The SBOM confirms tc358743.dtbo ships in the 2026-10-06 image.

The mainline Unicam driver matches only 'brcm,bcm2835-unicam-upstream' and supports only Media Controller.

Legacy driver: '{ .compatible = "brcm,bcm2835-unicam", .data = (void *)1 }, { .compatible = "brcm,bcm2835-unicam-legacy", .data = 0 }' and 'static int media_controller; module_param(media_controller...'. verification.final_statement: In rpi-6.18.y the downstream Unicam driver (Kconfig VIDEO_BCM2835_UNICAM_LEGACY) builds as bcm2835-unicam-legacy.ko. It matches 'brcm,bcm2835-unicam' (.data=1, which forces Media Controller mode) and 'brcm,bcm2835-unicam-legacy' (.data=0, where mode follows the media_controller module parameter, default 0). The BCM2712 processor page says 'Other CODECs run in software' (only HEVC decode is in hardware) and gives 'H264 1080p30 encode (from ISP) ~30–40% CPU'.

claims.statement: The GStreamer v4l2h264enc element ('V4L2 H.264 Encoder') lives in gst-plugins-good's sys/v4l2 plugin. It is registered at runtime through gst_v4l2_h264_enc_register when a matching V4L2 M2M encoder device is present.
claims.evidence: The source contains 'GST_DEBUG_CATEGORY_INIT (gst_v4l2_h264_enc_debug, "v4l2h264enc", 0, "V4L2 H.264 Encoder")', 'gst_v4l2_is_h264_enc (GstCaps * sink_caps, GstCaps * src_caps)' and 'gst_v4l2_h264_enc_register (GstPlugin * plugin, ...)'.

verification.final_statement: v4l2h264enc ('V4L2 H.264 Encoder') is in gst-plugins-good sys/v4l2. It is registered dynamically by gst_v4l2_probe_and_register(), which calls gst_v4l2_h264_enc_register for M2M devices whose caps pass gst_v4l2_is_h264_enc. claims.statement: autoboot.txt is an optional file in the first boot partition. It sets boot_partition, accepts the [all], [none] and [tryboot] filters, and supports tryboot_a_b=1, which loads the normal config.txt and boot.img from the selected partition. This is the firmware mechanism for fail-safe A/B OS updates.

The file 'supports the [all], [none], and [tryboot] conditional filters'. The [tryboot] filter 'is intended for use in autoboot.txt to select a different boot_partition in tryboot mode for fail-safe OS updates.' verification.final_statement: autoboot.txt is an optional file in the first boot partition that sets boot_partition. It accepts the [all], [none] and [tryboot] filters, and supports tryboot_a_b=1, which loads the normal config.txt and boot.img instead of tryboot.txt and tryboot.img. Combined with tryboot, it is the firmware mechanism for fail-safe A/B OS updates. The docs note it only picks the boot partition, and that a production A/B system also needs redundant partitions and update tooling (they point to Connect A/B and rpi-image-gen).
verification.notes: Checked verbatim. The page has no explicit list of supported models. EEPROM PARTITION_WALK supports this kind of A/B scheme on Pi 4 and Pi 5.

claims.statement: tryboot is triggered by adding 'tryboot' after the partition number in the reboot command. Raspberry Pi documents it as 'Fail-safe OS updates (tryboot)' for unattended or remote systems. When secure boot is enabled, tryboot mode loads tryboot.img instead of boot.img.
claims.source_title: Raspberry Pi Documentation - Raspberry Pi hardware (EEPROM boot flow)
claims.evidence: Quotes: 'To set the tryboot flag, add tryboot after the partition number in the reboot command.' 'This is useful for unattended or remote systems to ensure recovery from failed boots.' 'If secure-boot is enabled, then tryboot mode will cause tryboot.img to be loaded instead of boot.img.'

verification.final_statement: tryboot is set by adding 'tryboot' after the partition number in the reboot command, for example sudo reboot '0 tryboot'. It is documented under 'Fail-safe OS updates (tryboot)'. The one-shot flag loads tryboot.txt, or with tryboot_a_b the alternate partition's config.txt. Because the flag is cleared before the firmware starts, a crash or reset reverts to the original configuration. All models support tryboot, but Pi 4B rev 1.0/1.1 need an EEPROM that is not write-protected. With secure boot enabled, tryboot mode loads tryboot.img instead of boot.img.
verification.notes: The quote 'This is useful for unattended or remote systems to ensure recovery from failed boots' is in eeprom-bootloader.adoc line 162. It describes BOOT_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT, not tryboot, so the claim attaches it to the wrong feature. BOOT_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT is itself relevant to the appliance.

claims.statement: Some documented config.txt and bootloader settings affect boot time. initial_turbo runs the CPU in turbo from boot for up to 60 seconds or until cpufreq takes over. disable_splash=1 hides the rainbow splash. Network install's keyboard detection adds about 1 second to boot.
claims.source_title: Raspberry Pi Documentation - config.txt; Raspberry Pi hardware (bootloader configuration)
claims.evidence: Quotes: initial_turbo 'Enables turbo mode from boot for the given value in seconds, or until cpufreq sets a frequency. The maximum value is 60.' disable_splash: 'the rainbow splash screen will not be shown on boot'. Bootloader docs: 'network install must initialise the USB controller and enumerate devices. This increases boot time by approximately 1 second'.

verification.final_statement: Several documented settings affect boot time. initial_turbo enables turbo from boot for up to 60 seconds or until cpufreq sets a frequency, and the November 2024 firmware already changed its default from 0 to 60 'to reduce boot time', so on current firmware it is on by default rather than a tuning lever. disable_splash=1 hides the rainbow splash (default 0). Network-install keyboard detection adds about 1 second to boot. NET_INSTALL_ENABLED defaults to 1 on flagship boards since Pi 4B and to 0 on Compute Modules since CM4. BOOT_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT can reset a unit whose OS never starts.
verification.notes: overclocking.adoc lines 62-66 give the default change. A later table (line 290) still lists the default as 0, so the docs are internally inconsistent. The other quotes are in boot.adoc line 94 and eeprom-bootloader.adoc lines 495-503.

verification.final_statement: archive.raspberrypi.com publishes main/source/Sources (431197 bytes) and Sources.gz (120496 bytes) for trixie, and Sources.gz returns HTTP 200. Source for Raspberry Pi (+rpt) packages can therefore be fetched with apt deb-src.
verification.notes: Checked. I found no evidence of a snapshot service for archive.raspberrypi.com comparable to snapshot.debian.org.

claims.statement: Reasoning: the Pi 4 and CM4 run the same arm64 bcm2711 kernel (linux-image-rpi-v8), and the Pi 5 and CM5 run the same bcm2712 kernel (linux-image-rpi-2712), so a single Raspberry Pi OS image covers all four candidate targets. Only config.txt overlays (tc358743 vs tc358743-pi5, cam0/4lane) and storage layout (SD vs eMMC) change between them.
claims.source_title: Inference from G-06, G-12, G-13, G-59 (Buildroot bcm2711 DTS list includes bcm2711-rpi-cm4; bcm2712 used for CM5)
claims.evidence: Buildroot raspberrypi4_64_defconfig builds 'broadcom/bcm2711-rpi-4-b ... broadcom/bcm2711-rpi-cm4' from bcm2711_defconfig. The cm5io defconfig uses bcm2712 with 'bcm2712-rpi-cm5-cm5io'. The Lite image ships both rpi-v8 and rpi-2712 kernels.

verification.final_statement: This is reasoning built on verified inputs. The 2026-10-06 Lite image ships both the rpi-v8 (bcm2711, 4K pages) and rpi-2712 (16K pages) kernels, with module trees that include tc358743, unicam, rp1-cfe and bcm2835-codec, and device trees for Pi 4B, CM4, Pi 5, CM5 and CM5 Lite. The firmware loads kernel_2712.img on BCM2712 and kernel8.img otherwise, so one image can boot all four candidates. More than overlays and storage differs per board. The overlay differs (tc358743 vs tc358743-pi5), as do the cam0 and 4lane parameters. The capture model differs: Pi 4/CM4 default to legacy Unicam in video-node mode, while Pi 5/CM5 use CFE with Media Controller only. The encode path differs: hardware bcm2835-codec on Pi 4/CM4, software only on Pi 5/CM5. Lane count differs: the Pi 4B connector is 2-lane, which caps TC358743 at 1080p50 YUV422 or 1080p30 RGB888, while 4 lanes on a Compute Module give 1080p60. Storage and provisioning differ too (SD vs eMMC with rpiboot). config.txt [pi4]/[pi5]/[cm4]/[cm5] filters let one file hold the per-model settings.
verification.notes: The SBOM lists bcm2711-rpi-cm4*.dtb and bcm2712-rpi-cm5*/cm5l*.dtb and both module trees. boot.adoc line 24 covers the kernel fallback, csi-2-usage.adoc the TC358743 lane limits, and conditional.adoc lines 31-61 the filters. The original 'only overlays and storage change' understated the differences.

open_questions: Does TC358743 capture work on Pi 5 or CM5 through RP1-CFE with the tc358743-pi5 overlay, and at what formats (1080p60 UYVY in 2-lane vs 4-lane, at 486 vs 297 MHz link frequency)? To resolve: test on hardware with media-ctl/v4l2-ctl and check the raspberrypi/linux issues and forum threads for tc358743 plus CFE.

Which compatible do the default csi0/csi1 DT nodes and the tc358743 overlay use on Pi 4/CM4 in rpi-6.18.y? This decides whether the legacy video-node-centric Unicam driver or the MC-only mainline driver binds. To resolve: read bcm2711-rpi-ds.dtsi / bcm270x.dtsi and tc358743-overlay.dts in rpi-6.18.y, then check /sys/bus/platform/drivers on a running Pi 4.

Exact limits of the Pi 4/CM4 bcm2835-codec hardware H.264 encoder (max resolution, 1080p60 feasibility, H.264 level), and whether gst v4l2h264enc on Trixie with kernel 6.18 still works with DMABUF import from Unicam. To resolve: read the bcm2835-codec driver source (drivers/staging/vc04_services/bcm2835-codec) and benchmark.

CPU and thermal budget on Pi 5/CM5 for software x264 at 1080p60 while also recording, running RTMP (rtmp2sink) and WebRTC (webrtcbin). To resolve: benchmark x264 presets (ultrafast/superfast, zerolatency) on Pi 5/CM5 with active cooling.

Can rpi-image-gen pin package versions (for example via apt snapshot mirrors) so builds are bit-reproducible over time? The README only says 'reproducible'. To resolve: read the rpi-image-gen docs on apt sources and snapshots, or test two builds weeks apart and diff the SBOMs.

Does rpi-image-gen's image-rota layer use the firmware tryboot/autoboot.txt mechanism, and does it work on eMMC Compute Modules (CM4/CM5) as well as SD? To resolve: read docs/layer/image-rota.adoc and the rpi-connect-ota source.

Is Raspberry Pi Connect Remote Update still beta as of 2026-10, does it support CM4/CM5 and eMMC/NVMe, and can it run without Raspberry Pi's cloud (self-hosted)? To resolve: check the Raspberry Pi Connect documentation and the forum thread t=395798.
The exact device list for autoboot.txt/tryboot (whether CM5 and Pi 500 are explicitly listed). To resolve: read the complete autoboot.txt section of config_txt.adoc in raspberrypi/documentation.
Is camera_auto_detect=0 needed when only the tc358743 overlay is loaded (no sensor attached)? To resolve: test on hardware.

Measured boot-to-first-frame time for Raspberry Pi OS Lite (with cloud-init, NetworkManager etc.) vs a tuned Raspberry Pi OS image vs Buildroot on each candidate board. No primary source has comparable numbers. To resolve: measure with systemd-analyze plus a GPIO or serial timestamp at pipeline start.

How quickly does Buildroot's upstream Raspberry Pi defconfig move to the rpi-6.18.y kernel? It was still 6.12.61 in 2026.08. To resolve: track the Buildroot git log for configs/raspberrypi*_defconfig.

Security-update cadence for the Raspberry Pi-overridden packages (ffmpeg +rpt, gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad +rpt, plugins-base +rpt) compared with Debian security. To resolve: compare changelogs and dates on archive.raspberrypi.com against security-tracker.debian.org.

Does any part of the planned pipeline (for example closed-source ATEM SDK binaries or prebuilt libs) assume 4K pages and break on the Pi 5's 16K-page kernel? To resolve: test, or plan to use kernel8.img (4K pages) on Pi 5.

What CMA size will 1080p60 capture plus encoder buffers need? The defconfig CMA_SIZE_MBYTES=5 is overridden by the DT/vc4-kms overlay in practice. To resolve: read /proc/meminfo CmaTotal on Trixie and the cma overlay documentation.
gaps: There are no measured boot-time, RAM or rootfs-size numbers for a PACSCORDER-equivalent build, either for an rpi-image-gen minbase build with GStreamer, ffmpeg and x264 or for Buildroot with the same packages. Building and timing both on the chosen board is the only way to settle points 3 and 4.

Can archive.raspberrypi.com be pinned in time (a snapshot service, or retention of old .debs)? rpi-image-gen ships a snapshot.debian.org layer (debian-trixie-arm64-minbase-snapshot) for the Debian half only. The archive does keep old versioned kernel packages (6.12.25 and later), but I found no documented policy for the other +rpt packages. Resolve by asking Raspberry Pi, or plan an aptly or reprepro mirror.

What do Raspberry Pi's +rpt patches to ffmpeg (8:7.1.5-0+deb13u1+rpt2), gstreamer1.0-plugins-base and gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad (+rpt4) actually change, for example V4L2 M2M, DRM PRIME or DMABUF fixes? This decides whether Buildroot's stock GStreamer 1.24.13 and FFmpeg 6.1.5 match the Raspberry Pi OS media path. Resolve by diffing the source packages from main/source/Sources.

Raspberry Pi has no formal support horizon for Raspberry Pi OS Trixie's kernel, firmware and +rpt packages. Debian 13's dates (2028 full support, 2030 LTS) do not automatically cover them, and the only commitment found for the legacy OS is a staff blog comment about critical kernel fixes.

Does Raspberry Pi Connect Remote Update A/B support Compute Modules (CM4/CM5 on eMMC)? The docs say 'Raspberry Pi 4 or later', Imager offers only Pi 4 or Pi 5 device types, and rpi-image-gen v2.3.0 says image-rota 'enforces device compatibility' with CM4/CM5 Lite defaulting to SD. Is the feature still beta?

Does the tc358743-pi5 overlay support 4 lanes on the Pi 5 board's 22-pin connectors, not just on Compute Module CAM1? The README text was copied from the Pi 4 entry. Does tc358743-audio work on Pi 5/CM5, given it uses compatible brcm,bcm2835 and the i2s_clk_consumer label?

Software H.264 encode on Pi 5/CM5: the docs give about 30-40% CPU for 1080p30 from the ISP. There are no figures for 1080p50/60 from TC358743 with simultaneous recording, RTMP and WebRTC, and no data on encoder latency. This drives the platform choice more than the OS choice.

H.264 patent licensing for software encoding (x264 or libavcodec) on Pi 5/CM5 has not been examined, and neither has Raspberry Pi's licensing position for the Pi 4 hardware encoder. The licence-compliance comparison covers only copyright and GPL.
Does Buildroot 2025.02.x LTS include CM5 defconfigs and a kernel that supports the RP1 CFE and tc358743-pi5 overlay? This matters if the LTS branch is chosen for long-term maintenance.

Production hardening steps on Raspberry Pi OS that the comparison omits: masking rpi-eeprom-update or setting the bootloader FREEZE_VERSION (the service updates the EEPROM at boot), BOOT_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT, removing or disabling the preinstalled cloud-init, rpi-connect-lite and rpi-update, and the EDID provisioning step (v4l2-ctl --set-edid), which the TC358743 needs on every boot.

Is rpi-image-gen v2.8.0's SBOM or CVE output usable for GPL source-offer generation, i.e. does it map binaries to exact source packages and versions across both the Debian and RPi archives? Not tested.
Yocto (meta-raspberrypi) was not evaluated as a third option, though it sits between the two in reproducibility and update tooling.
design_risks: Pi 5 and CM5 have no hardware H.264 encoder (G-22). On those boards, recording plus RTMP plus WebRTC all depend on software x264 (G-30), which drives CPU, thermal and power design. Pi 4/CM4 have bcm2835-codec (G-18), but on Pi 4-class silicon only (reasoning).

The capture path differs by platform. Pi 4/CM4 use Unicam with an optional video-node mode (G-12, G-21). Pi 5/CM5 use RP1-CFE with the tc358743-pi5 overlay (G-13), which has no media-controller switch and so presumably needs media-ctl pipeline setup (reasoning). Bring-up code and EDID/DV-timings handling should be written once for MC-centric operation.

The kernel series changed within the Trixie release, from 6.12.75 to 6.18.34 (G-05). A fleet running 'apt full-upgrade' (G-08) can therefore move to a new kernel series unattended. Kernel and firmware packages should be held, or the fleet moved to image-based A/B updates (G-41, G-50).
rpi-update is installed in the stock Lite image (G-10), and Raspberry Pi warns it can leave a system unbootable (G-09). It should be removed from production images.
rpi-image-gen is young: first tagged release 2025-09-01 (G-37), and minor versions still break things (G-44). Builds need a pinned tag and a regression process for every upgrade.

Raspberry Pi Connect Remote Update OTA is beta and, as documented, requires Pi 4/5 on Ethernet with an SD card (G-43). The CM4/CM5 eMMC OTA story should not depend on it until that is confirmed (see open questions).

The raspi-config overlay root uses a tmpfs upper layer (G-48), so every write is lost on reboot and consumes RAM. Recordings, configuration and logs need a separate persistent data partition, and RAM must be budgeted (reasoning).

Buildroot's upstream Raspberry Pi defconfigs trail Raspberry Pi OS by one kernel series (6.12.61 vs 6.18.50) (G-59). They use 4K pages on Pi 5 (G-60) and do not install overlays on the Pi 5 defconfig (G-61). Buildroot results may not match Raspberry Pi's own testing.

Secure boot provisioning writes OTP on the SoC (customer key hash) (G-45, G-46), which cannot be undone. Signing-key custody and a test fleet are needed before it is enabled on production CM4/CM5 units (reasoning).

Licensing: shipping ffmpeg/GStreamer with x264 (GPL) requires source-offer compliance on either base. Raspberry Pi OS pulls from two archives (Debian plus archive.raspberrypi.com +rpt overrides, G-27, G-29, G-31), so compliance means tracking both source origins (G-70). Buildroot's legal-info is not complete on its own either (G-68).

Major Raspberry Pi OS versions are not upgraded in place (G-55), and a new one arrives every two years (G-56). The next one (Debian 14, presumably 2027) will require a full image rebuild and requalification. Debian 13 standard support ends 2028-08-09 (G-03).
G-raspberry-pi-os.comparison:
Raspberry Pi OS Lite, with rpi-image-gen for production builds, compared with Buildroot for PACSCORDER. Facts reference claim ids; anything labelled OPINION is my judgement.

1. Bring-up speed. Raspberry Pi OS Lite boots on all four candidate boards from one image (G-33, G-71). Its kernel already builds every module the pipeline needs: TC358743, Unicam, RP1-CFE and bcm2835-codec (G-16, G-17, G-18). The tc358743, tc358743-pi5 and tc358743-audio overlays ship with the kernel and are enabled in /boot/firmware/config.txt (G-11 to G-14). v4l-utils (v4l2-ctl, media-ctl) is preinstalled (G-24). i2c-tools, GStreamer good/bad/nice and ffmpeg/x264 are one apt install away (G-25 to G-31). Buildroot can build the same components (G-63, G-64, G-65), but each needs a config change and a cross-build, and its Pi 5 defconfig leaves overlays out by default (G-61). OPINION: Raspberry Pi OS Lite is much faster for first light on hardware that does not exist yet, especially while the platform is still undecided.

2. Kernel and driver parity with official overlays. Raspberry Pi OS tracks Raspberry Pi's current kernel, 6.18.50 (G-04), as apt packages built from the default rpi-6.18.y branch (G-06, G-07, G-16). Buildroot 2026.08 pins an older Raspberry Pi kernel commit, 6.12.61 (G-59). It also switches the Pi 5 kernel to 4K pages, unlike Raspberry Pi OS's 16K (G-20, G-60). Both kernels do build the TC358743 and CSI drivers (G-63). OPINION: Raspberry Pi OS gives exact parity with the kernel, firmware and overlays that Raspberry Pi tests. Buildroot can match it only if you maintain your own kernel pin and fragments.

3. Image size. Raspberry Pi OS Lite is 550 MB compressed and expands to about 3.08 GB with 633 packages (G-32, G-33). Buildroot's reference Raspberry Pi defconfigs build a 120M ext4 root filesystem (G-62). rpi-image-gen can build slimmer images; its announcement shows a 'slim' example (G-36). OPINION: Buildroot will produce the smallest image. An rpi-image-gen minbase build can close much of the gap, but a Debian image will stay larger. On 8–32 GB eMMC or SD this is unlikely to decide anything.

4. Boot time. No measured comparison exists in primary sources (see open questions). Raspberry Pi documents a few firmware levers, such as initial_turbo, disable_splash and the cost of network-install keyboard detection (G-54). Stock Lite also runs cloud-init, NetworkManager and netplan (G-32). OPINION: Buildroot with BusyBox init or a trimmed systemd will usually boot faster than stock Lite, and a trimmed rpi-image-gen image will land between the two. Measure before deciding.

5. Reproducibility. Official Raspberry Pi OS images record the pi-gen commit and ship an SPDX SBOM (G-34, G-35). rpi-image-gen describes itself as producing reproducible artefacts with SBOM and CVE reports (G-39, G-40), but it builds from live apt archives. Whether versions can be pinned over time is an open question. Buildroot pins every package version and hash in its tree (G-59, G-64), but bit-identical output is experimental and only works with the same output directory (G-66). OPINION: Buildroot gives stronger source-level reproducibility out of the box. rpi-image-gen gives a good SBOM and audit trail but needs a mirror or snapshot strategy to reach the same level.

6. OTA and updates. Raspberry Pi OS supports apt updates (G-08), but these can move a fleet onto a new kernel series (G-05). The production-grade options are the firmware's tryboot/autoboot.txt A/B mechanism (G-50, G-51), rpi-image-gen's image-rota (immutable A/B, EROFS, dm-verity, LUKS2, slot-shared data; G-41) and Raspberry Pi Connect Remote Update, which is beta and limited to Pi 4/5 on Ethernet with SD (G-42, G-43, G-53). The raspi-config overlay root (G-48) and the RAUC, SWUpdate and Mender packages in Debian (G-49) are also available. Buildroot offers no package updates by design and recommends whole-image upgrades (G-67), with RAUC, SWUpdate and Mender packaged (G-64). OPINION: both bases end up image-based. rpi-image-gen plus image-rota now gives Raspberry Pi OS an officially supported path, though it is young (G-37, G-44). Buildroot plus RAUC or SWUpdate is the more established embedded pattern but needs more integration work.

7. Licence compliance effort. Raspberry Pi OS draws on Debian and archive.raspberrypi.com, both of which publish source indexes (G-70), and each image ships an SBOM (G-34). Several media packages come from Raspberry Pi's own +rpt builds (G-27, G-29, G-31), so source must be tracked from two origins. Buildroot's make legal-info collects sources, patches, licences and a manifest, but by its own account is incomplete and must be reviewed (G-68). Both bases carry the same proprietary Raspberry Pi firmware blobs (G-69). OPINION: with x264 (GPL) in the product, the effort is similar. Buildroot's legal-info bundle is the easier artefact to hand over, while Raspberry Pi OS needs a tool-assisted export of sources from the SBOM.

8. Long-term maintenance. Raspberry Pi OS follows Debian, with a new major version every two years (G-56) and no supported in-place major upgrade (G-55). Debian 13 has standard support to 2028-08-09 and LTS to 2030-06-30 (G-03). Security fixes arrive through apt, and Raspberry Pi maintains the kernel and firmware (G-04, G-08). Buildroot's LTS branch (2025.02.x) lasts to March 2028 (G-58), but the board kernel and BSP stay your responsibility (G-59). OPINION: a small team carries less BSP and CVE work on Raspberry Pi OS plus rpi-image-gen. Buildroot makes sense when image size, boot time or a fully controlled bill of materials outweigh that burden.

Overall OPINION: start bring-up and platform selection on Raspberry Pi OS Lite (Trixie, kernel 6.18). Build production images with a pinned rpi-image-gen tag, using an image-rota A/B layout or a tryboot-based A/B scheme, a persistent data partition, held kernel and firmware packages, rpi-update removed, and secure boot provisioned with rpi-sb-provisioner on CM4/CM5. Revisit Buildroot only if measured boot time or footprint misses the product requirements.
G-raspberry-pi-os.comparison_critique:
Overall the comparison is fair, and it labels most judgements as opinion. Several points rest on outdated or misattributed facts, though, and some framing favours Raspberry Pi OS.

(1) Bring-up. The strongest evidence is missing from the text. The 2026-10-06 image's SBOM shows that tc358743.ko, unicam (legacy and mainline), rp1-cfe, pisp-be, bcm2835-codec and the tc358743, tc358743-pi5 and tc358743-audio .dtbo files actually ship for both kernels. Cite that, not just the defconfigs. Three things are misstated or omitted:
- 'Overlays are enabled in config.txt' is wrong. None is on by default; each needs a dtoverlay= line.
- bcm2835-codec is listed as a pipeline module, but it is useless on Pi 5/CM5. Those boards encode in software only (about 30-40% CPU for 1080p30 per the BCM2712 docs).
- Capture differs by board. Pi 4/CM4 default to legacy Unicam in video-node mode, while Pi 5/CM5 CFE is Media Controller only and needs media-ctl. Bring-up therefore differs per board whichever OS is chosen.

There is a fair Buildroot gotcha the comparison could add: BR2_PACKAGE_GST1_PLUGINS_GOOD_PLUGIN_V4L2_PROBE is off by default, so v4l2h264enc is absent until it is enabled. Turning on overlays for the Pi 5 defconfig, by contrast, is a one-line change, and presenting it as a burden overstates the cost.

(2) Kernel parity. 6.18.50 vs 6.12.61 is accurate, but the gap is mostly the age of Buildroot's pin (a firmware and kernel snapshot built about 2025-12-08), not the series. Raspberry Pi still ships rpi-6.12 kernels (6.12.109 in the 2026-10-06 Bookworm legacy image), so a Buildroot user can bump the pin. Calling 4K pages a parity defect is biased. Raspberry Pi's own docs say kernel8.img (4K) runs on BCM2712 and is the firmware fallback. The comparison also skips userland parity: Buildroot 2026.08 has GStreamer 1.24.13 and FFmpeg 6.1.5, while Raspberry Pi OS has 1.26.2 and 7.1.5 with unexamined +rpt patches. That point favours Raspberry Pi OS more strongly than the kernel argument does.

(3) Image size. This compares unlike things. 120M is Buildroot's minimal BusyBox reference, not a media appliance, and 3.08 GB is the raw Lite image size, not used space. 'Unlikely to decide anything on 8–32 GB' is not supported. image-rota duplicates the system slot, Connect A/B requires at least 16 GB, and CM4 comes with 8 GB eMMC, so size does interact with the A/B choice.

(4) Boot time. Correctly marked as unmeasured. However, initial_turbo is not a lever: the November 2024 firmware already made 60 the default. NET_INSTALL defaults to off on Compute Modules.

(5) Reproducibility. The 'open question' is half answered. rpi-image-gen ships a snapshot.debian.org-based trixie minbase layer, but I found nothing equivalent for archive.raspberrypi.com (kernel, firmware, +rpt media packages), so a private mirror is still needed for that half. rpi-image-gen also supports only native arm64 Debian hosts; containers and x86 QEMU are 'not formally supported', which affects CI. Buildroot's RPi defconfigs enforce download hashes (BR2_DOWNLOAD_FORCE_CHECK_HASHES=y), which strengthens the Buildroot side.

(6) OTA. The Connect Remote Update description is out of date. Current docs require 'Raspberry Pi 4 or later', an internet connection (not specifically Ethernet) and a storage device, typically microSD, of at least 16 GB. Organisation accounts can deploy to offline devices, and the docs no longer say beta. The 'young' judgement is fair and has concrete support: v2.8.0 fixed A/B slots sharing one baked-in SSH host key and NetworkManager state not persisting, and minor releases break configs (G-44). One more risk is missing: apt full-upgrade or rpi-update can also change the bootloader EEPROM (the rpi-eeprom-update service, and rpi-update on Pi 4/5).

(7) Licence compliance. 'Same proprietary blobs' overstates it: they are equivalent files at different versions. Buildroot also mislabels LICENCE.broadcom as BSD-3-Clause when it is a binary-only, Raspberry-Pi-use-restricted licence, which shows why legal-info output needs review. H.264 patent licensing for software x264 encoding on Pi 5/CM5 is not considered at all, and it applies to both bases.

(8) Maintenance. Applying Debian 13's 2028 and 2030 dates to Raspberry Pi OS is unsupported for the kernel, firmware and +rpt packages. The only Raspberry Pi commitment found is a staff comment about critical kernel fixes for the legacy OS. In practice, Bookworm legacy images are still refreshed a year on, but that is observed behaviour, not policy. Buildroot's stable branches last about three months, and 2026.05 is already end of life. The comparison omits whether 2025.02 LTS supports CM5 and CFE.

Recommendation. Starting bring-up on Raspberry Pi OS Lite is well supported. One part of the production recipe is internally inconsistent: 'held kernel and firmware packages' does nothing on an immutable image-rota or EROFS root, and holding trixie kernel packages freezes them without fixes (the trixie archive has no 6.12 build after 6.12.75). Pinning has to happen at image-build time through mirrored or snapshotted archives and a pinned rpi-image-gen tag. Note also that the official Compute Module docs still point to pi-gen, not rpi-image-gen, for customising CM images. That is a minor sign that rpi-image-gen's official positioning is not yet settled.
